Pushti Marg means the path of grace. Pushti Marg means the path of attaining Bhagwan through grace. The foundation of Pushti Marg is Hari-Guru Vaishnav. Pushti Marg is the path of love, seva and remembrance. Pushti Marg is experienced when one has dinta (humbleness). Pusti Marg is the path of pure Prem-Lakshana Bhakti, i.e. Bhakti manifested with Supreme Love. Bhagwan manifested Pusti Marg to have His seva performed by pusti souls. The four human attainments sanctioned in the scriptures are – Dharm, Arth (wealth), Kama (desire) and Moksh (liberation). In Pusti Marg 'Dharm' is service of God Shri Thakurji, 'Wealth' is Shri Thakurji himself. 'Desire' is the craving for His glimpses and 'Liberation' is always to remain in the presence of Shri Krishna. Seva (service) and remembrance are the sacred duties of all devotees in Pusti Marg. When seva and remembrance are done lovingly with selfless humbleness, Shri Thakurji pleases and bestows His grace. One should always see the divinity in all vishnavs and maintain relations "lovingly with humbleness". One should always see only the good qualities in a vaishnav, without giving any attention to their faults and should never criticize them. One should consider Shri Mahaprabhuji and Shri Thakurji (Baghwan) to be one and the same, and should not differentiate between them. The descendents of Shri Mahaprabhuji are all divine manifestations; hence they should be regarded as Guru. One is initiated and accepted into Pusti Marg only by these descendents as Gurus. Surrender exclusively to Pushti Prabhu (Bhagwan, the supreme one) and refrain from seeking aashray (shelter) anywhere else. 'Brahm Sambandh' is an initiation to re-establish our relationship with Prabhu (Purnaprusotham) from whom we are separated, as a humble servant. We surrender to Shri Thakurji, our egos and attachments through this initation. By surrendering our selves, we get freed from egos and worldly attachments. Satsang is the compulsory duty of pusti souls. Through satsang, our bhava (divine sentiments) becomes enriched and steadfast. One should never lose faith in Prabhu (Shri Thakurji). Both, in happiness as well as in distressful adversities, one should keep full faith in Prabhu. Through steadfast faith (ananya aashray), our exclusive aashray in Pushti Prabhu is perfected. Through seva, performed with total love, an unwavering and abiding attachment for Thakurji develops. This divine attachment purifies and sanctifies the heart which becomes increasingly sensitive to sublime sentiments. This state is called Vyasan (addiction), and by it, viprayog state (craving for ShriThakurji is perfected when one experiences Prabhu's lila in the inner heart. 1 continued

Rules of conduct in Pushti Marg are in accordance with scriptural laws of Sanatan Dharm, which hold a position of great importance. It is said that rules of conduct are the foremost of ones' duties. The reason for this is that every human being brings with him a vast range of desires at birth itself. The fulfillment of these desires is a birth right as well as a duty. On understanding this, the question arises as to how these desires can be satisfied. To avoid the spread of chaos due to stealing, plundering, violence, etc., saints and sages of ancient times contemplated deeply on this to determine as to how to structure a disciplined society. What is the proper daily routine? What is appropriate behavior and what is inappropriate behavior? After deep contemplation, a number of treatises were written containing the teachings of a disciplined life, appropriate behavior, inappropriate behavior, corrupted behavior, etc. and a delineation of rules of conduct. Originally, these rules of conduct were practiced only by high caste Brahmins, but by SHRI MAHAPRABHUJI'S grace, those from the other three castes also began to practice them. Through these rules of conduct, the Bhavatmak oneness of all the four divisions of caste were established and became stable in Pushti Marg. In the tretises on conduct, mother, father and teacher were supposed to give trainng to the children at a young age. It is said 'mother is Bhagavan, Father is Bhagavan. Teacher is Bhagavan'. It should be understood that just as moist earth can be shaped into a pot, similarly a child will behave according to the rules of conduct that are taught to him at an early age. Accordingly, it is said that proper rules of conduct is of atmost importance. The code of ethics of ancient times has deteriorated over the course of time and all guidelines have been destroyed in present era. “Yedha yedha hi dharmas-siya ghala-niir-bhavti bharatah Dharma sans-tha-panar-tha-yah sam-bhava-mi yuge yuge” In one of the famous shlokas from Bhagavad Gita, Shri Krishna has told to Arjun 'In every yuga, whenever dharm is destroyed, Bhagavan will take a divine Avtaar (birth) to re-establish the Dharm'. According to that law, Srimad Vallabhacharya manifested in a divine Avtaar (birth), to re-establish the pure Vedic values and spread the teachings for the highest realization. Seeing the imperfectness of human souls, Mahaprabhuji felt deeply worried and became lost in contemplation. He questioned himself. “How can the fault pervaded soul experience the unblemished perfection of Purnaprushotam?” At that time Prabhu appeared before him and ordained, 'I will remove the five innate faults of anyone to whom you would give 'brahm sambandh'. The five type of faults are due to natural, place, time coincidence and touch manifestation. “Aaniya-tha sarvah dho-shanam na niv-ra-tih kan-tha-chan Aa-samar-pitham vastunam tasmadh: varjan-ma-cha-ketah” Further, he stated 'Other than surrendering all things, there is no way to remove the innate faults. Therefore, one should abstain from using any thing which has not been surrendered to Him first. The question then arose as to what could be the correct rules of living to establish and maintain this way of surrender. For developing this in his sevaks, Srimad Vallabhacharya prescribed rules for a dedicated life with devotion and on that, his teachings are founded. By living according to these guidelines, one will become physically and mentally disciplined and purified and will become worthy and capable to perform seva of the ultimate supreme, Parabrahm. In the early days of Pushti Marg, "after taking 'Brahm Sambandh', vaishnavs used to ask, 'What is my duty?' At that time either the guru himself or a scholar of Pushti Marg would teach the vaishnav the rules and methods of seva and remembrance. These teachings have been forgotten these days hence once again they should be understood and followed. 2

The name of our sect is Pushti Marg. The 'Principal Guru' of every vaishnav is Srimad Vallabhacharya Mahaprabhuji. Every descendent of Sri Mahaprabhuji is 'guru-dwar', meaning they symbolize 'Him' as Guru. The Goswami from whom we have taker 'Brahm Sambandh' initiation is our Guru. Although Brahm Sambandh initiation may have been taken from any particular Goswami, still every descendent of Shri Mahaprabhuji should in every way, be given equal regards and should be worshiped as Guru by vaishnav. 'Brahm Sambndh' or 'Atma Nivedan' is given when one bathes in 'apares' and with Tulsi in hands pronounces 'Gadya Mantra', as would be told by Guru in front of Shri Thakurji. Then tulsi leaves are offered to Prabhu's lotus feet. In Pusti Marg only male Goswami descendents of Srimad Vallabhacharya are qualified to give Ashtakshar Maha Mantra and Brahm Sambandh initiation. In pustimarg, traditional seat of Guru is not passed on to disciples and therefore, initiation should be taken only from a descendent male Goswami. Many people mistakenly refer to fasting as 'apvas' but the correct word is 'upvas' Apvas means to reside in hell and 'upvas' means to reside near Thakurji. Hence the correct word 'upvas' should be used. After taking Ashtakshar Mantra and Brahm Sambandh initiation, a vaishnav should greet each vaishnav by saying '||JAI SHRI KRISHNA||'. In writing a letter to a vaishnav, one should use the greeting “||JAI SHRI KRISHNA||”. Even if the vaishnav is our relative and older than us, '||JAI SHRI KRISHNA||' is to be used in conversation. It is not the tradition to greet a Goswami with '||JAI SHRI KRISHNA||'. The reason is that a sevak does not have the worthiness to convey Bhagavad remembrance to the Guru. Through the grace of the guru, the sevak has obtained Bhagavad remembrance. In meeting a Goswami, one should say 'dandvat'. In writing a letter 'Sashtang Dandvat Pranam' should be written and on the phone my 'Sashtang Dandvat Pranam' should be spoken to be followed by any other matters. Panchang Dandvat is done before Thakurji and Sashtang Dandvat is done before Gurudev. Females do not do Sashtang Dandvat. Before going to one's Guru or any Goswami, one should first say 'Dandvat' and then do pranam. After this, one should ask 'May I take charan sparsh?'. After receiving permission, one should touch both feet with the right hand and then with that hand one touches one's own both eyes, forehead and heart. In seva or in any work being done for a goswami that does not require two hands, one should use only the right hand and not the left hand Accordingly, touching of the feet is done with the right hand only. Thakurji's and Gurudev's touching of the feet is done in the following manner. Place the left hand under the right forearm and then with the right palm in the upwards position, very softly touch the left charan (foot), then the right, then again the left. One should not sit before the guru with crossed arms. One should not sit with feet extended towards guru and also should not sit with his back behind him. One should not touch the guru's cushion or cloth spread beneath him. The feet should not be kept in an upwards position or in any other undisciplined manner. One should sit with crossed legs in a well mannered way and with humbleness. One should be careful at all times that one's feet should never touch the guru's cushion pillow, clothing, the bed spread or any of his things. When the guru is sitting at a higher level, one should not sit at the same level but should sit at a lower level. If the guru is sitting on a chair one should not sit on a chair. In the presence of the guru, a well-learned person, a person of royalty or any other highly placed person should not keep an attitude of self importance. One should not pass wind in the guru's presence. One should not sing or hum film songs or other such things loudly in the guru’s presence. While in the guru's presence, vaishnavas should not discuss household matters or any other wo

Daily one should wake up at 4-00 a.m., bathe and then sit in Bhagavad remembrance repetition of mantra, etc. 4-00 a.m. is the time of brahmmuhurt and is said to be the time divine nectar. During that period while sitting in Bhagavad remembrance, one is able to have better concentration in every way. In addition the wind which blows during that period contains divine immortal nectar and if one is in the waking state, the life span is increased, good health is obtained, strength increases, the capacity of the sense organs increases and memory becomes stronger. If one is not able to wake up at 4-00 a.m. then at the latest, one should be awaken before sunrise. Rising after sunrise causes harm to the memory, sense organs, intellect, strength, health and life-span. Symptoms of 'Tamoguna', laziness, carelessness, anger, indiscipline etc. arise. All actions in a vaishnav's life should be dedicated to Prabhu. To establish this, the following four habits should be cultivated. The very first thing, upon rising, one should have darshan of Prabhu's picture kept in the room and then take charan sparsh. Before writing any thing one should first write 'ashtakshar mantra”. Before speaking any thing one should first say 'Jai Shri Krishna'. Before thinking upon any worldly matters, sitting on the bed one mala of ashtakshar mantra should be done in mind. After brushing teeth and before taking tea, coffee, milk, etc. one should first take prasad, tulsi, bidi (prasadi sopari) or any other prasad in a small quantity. One should not become angry in the morning. Refrain from any thoughts which would give rise to enmity, jealousy, arrogance etc. Do not engage in useless talks. With determination, remove any thoughts of worry from the mind. Do not speak untruths. Do not quarrel with any one in the house or any outsider and do not use profanity with anyone. The entire mood of the day depends upon how the morning is spent, therefore, keep the morning time pure and mellow so that the entire day up to night will pass beautifully. Vaishnavs should strictly abide by the rule: bathing after going to the toilet. If one is unable to take a full bath and wash the hair, one should, at least bathe to the neck. Whatever clothing has been worn while going to the toilet should not be touched after bath or bring in contract with any other clothing and it should be immersed in water before touching or wearing. By doing this, one will avoid the offence of doing any seva related work in the impure state. Every vaishnav should have Thakurji's seva in their home. If possible one should have 'Swarup Seva' but if that is not possible then have 'Chitra Seva'. But in any case, Thakurji's seva should be performed at home. Every family member from youngest to eldest who has taken 'Brahm Sambandh' should keep a firm resolve to take charan sparsh of Thakurji in the seva which is performed in the home. Those without brahm sambandh should keep firm resolve for darshan and dandvat. Any food should only be taken after charan sparsh or darshan and dandvat. To whatever extent possible, each of the family members, including youngsters and aged should participate in seva. 4

There are countless rules necessary for keeping good health by which physical vitality is maintained. In the same way, there are innumerable rules related to food for keeping purity of the soul. Purity of the soul is necessary for seva, devotion, remembrance and other such activities. Vaishnavs should abstain from eating all such things which have been forbidden in the scriputres, Viz.. Meat, eggs, food prepared with eggs, alchohol and other intoxicating substances, onion and garlic. These are strictly prohibited all the times. To whatever extent possible, vaishnavs should try to abstain from eating in restaurants. Impure food eaten in restaurants destroys the entire intellect, especially the decision making faculty which judges right and wrong and good health required for seva can not be maintained. To whatever extent possible, vaishnavs should not take food or water in the homes of non vaishnavs as it destroys devotional bhava. Those foods which may be considered to promote good health but which are harmful to the soul should be avoided. Likewise those things beneficial for the soul but which may be harmful to the health should be avoided. (For example, sweets offered to Thakurji should not be taken by a diabetic). 5

While performing seva, one should not become angry with anyone. During the period of seva one should only discuss bhagavad related matters. During the time of performing seva, one should make constant efforts to absorb the mind deeply in Prabhu and in seva. One should keep control over the mind and remain vigilant to avoid thinking of worldly matters. During seva, one should not quarrel with any family member or neighbor and should abstain from any action which will cause arguments. One should not, at any time, use profanity, speak arrogantly or insultingly. Seva should be performed with total concentration, with a free untroubled mind and with bhava. One should not do seva with laziness, carelessness or insincerity. If ever our religion, Pushti Marg, Pushti Purushottam Prabhu, Goswami Gurus or Vaishanvs are being criticized in our presence and one is capable, it should be opposed in such a way so as not to cause any argument. If this is not possible, one should immediately leave that place to avoid hearing of such criticism. Whenever facing adversities, one should not become agitated and seek solutions not sanctioned in Pusti Marg. One should keep a firm unwavering aashray in Pushti Purushottam Prabhu. After completing the mandatory daily activities one should not waste time unproductively but remain busy in seva remembrance, repetition of mantra, recitation of kirtan, listening to discourses, satsang, darshan, dharm, reading books on bhakti and knowledge etc. 6

One should maintain respect for religious books in every way. One should not touch religious books with the feet. One should not put religious books in a place where food is taken or any such other impure place. While keeping a religious book down, it should be put down gently and carefully in an appropriate place. It should not be tossed or dropped disrespectfully. One should not touch a religious book with an impure hand. One should not read religious books while eating, while in a reclining position,while wearing shoes, without bathing after going to the toilet, during sutak, during monthly period or in any other impure state. These books embody the actual form of Thakurji and His Lila and should be respected accordingly. Religious books should be read in a pure state revering them to be Thakurji's own form. They should be read as much as possible, carefully without rushing and with sincere inquisitiveness. Considering them to be our valuable wealth religious books should be preserved with appropriate care. 7

t: VAISHNAV FASTS AND RULES OF FASTING
x: Vaishnavs are required to observe fortnightly ekadisi fast and also four Bhagavad avtaar manifestation days (1) Janamashtmi, (2) Ramnomi, (3) Narsingh Jayanti and (4) Vaman Jayanti. These fasts should be observed strictly according to the prescribed rules. The day of ekadisi some times overlaps on two days. If so, refer tippani (panchang) for ascertaining the correct day. One should awake before sunrise on the day of fast. After bathing, one should engage in Bhagavad remembrance, repetition of name, recitation etc. One should not take any addictive substance on the day of a fast. On the day of a fast, one should not watch T.V. Video, film, etc. or any such worldly entertainments. On the day of fasting, one should remain celebrate. Except for mandatory seva related matters and Bhagavad name one should remain silent. Foods such as gains, lentils, radish, onion, garlic, all salt other than rock salt, hing, red chili, fenugreek, (methi seeds), jagary, tumeric, mustad seeds, seasum seed, pan leaves, popcorn, puffed rice, pressed rice, vegetable oil refind products, any thing spoiled, or food remains after eating from a vessel are prohibited and should not be consumed on the day of a fast. Allowed foods are milk, foods made from milk as yogurt, butter milk, butter, ghee, vegetables: Dudhi, parval, potato, suran, ratalu (kand), sweet potato, arbi, green chilli, Coriander, ginger, dried ginger, (sonth), lemon, fruit, cumin (jhira), dried fruits and nut, sago, (tapica, sabudana), rock salt, (sendha naman), surar, rock sugar (misri), black pepper, clove, cardamom, (elaichi) rajgaro, coconut, peanut, hringara, buckwheat, arrowroot and sama. Any of the items from the above list may be used for preparing food on a day of fasting. On the day of a fast, one may lie down in the afternoon but should not sleep. To whatever extent possible one should be absorbed in Bhagavad remembrance, kirtan, repetition of name, recitation etc. On the day of a fast, one should not over eat or eat for pleasure or but, should eat just enough to sufficiently nourish the body. One should not eat in such a way so as to cause laziness, sleepiness or feeling of heaviness. To whatever extent possible, one should take only milk, yogurt, buttermilk, fruits and fruit juice. To whatever extent possible, one should abstain from worldly relations and activities on the day of fast and remain absorbed in seva and devotion so that one's time will pass fruitfully. 8

Children should arise at the latest by 5-30 a.m. After rising early, wash hands, face and brush teeth. Recite Mangalacharan in remembrance of Prabhu and Guru and then begin one's regular studies. Daily, first thing in the morning with folded hands, say Jai Shri Krishna to the mother, father, brothers, sisters, elders etc. Daily each morning, after bathing, recite Sarvotam Stotram, Yamunashtak, Krishnaashra; Navratna, Siddhant Rahasya, etc. Do one mala of ashtakshar mantra repetition. This should be done without rushing and with a peaceful mind with correct pronounciation. Before going to school, college, classes etc. first do dandvat to Shri Thakurji. Do not wear shoes inside the house. At home or outside, even by mistake, do not consume prohibited foods, alcohol etc.' On fortnightly ekadasi or Puhti Margiya sacred festival days, abstain from watching T. V., films video, etc... and also abstain from going to clubs, hotels or eating in restaurants. If there is Thakurji's seva being performed in the home, set aside some time each day to help in seva. One should wear two tulsi malas and should not to remain without them even for a moment. Keep Shri Maha Prabhuji's, Gurudev and Thakurji's pictures on one's study desk or in one's study area in the house for darshan and also keep a set of pictures in one's bag to take to school or college. During daily studies or during exams., one should not do any copying or cheating. One should not have one's lessons written by another person. One should strive constantly with determination to attain top marks. One should keep one's study books with extreme care, and should not put them wherever one pleases. Do not sit in such a way so that one's feet will touch any of these books. Do not form habit of reading while lying down or on the back with the book resting on the chest. Do not read in such a way as to cause damage to the book. For the purpose of memorization, do not speak or sing song lessons hurriedly without correct pronunciation, do not shake the head, feet or hands and do not memorize like a parrot without understanding etc. All of these bad habits weaken the memory and intellectual power and should not be used. One should keep up with one's studies daily, work consistently and not uselessly stay up all night cramming before exams. If one has made a mistake, big or small, one should take the matter to one's parents or Gurudev (teacher) and never try to hide any thing from them. Without any delay, one should seek immediate appropriate guidance from them. After studying conscientiously, one needs to engage in sports, play and entertaining activities also, but, these should not distract one's mind during the study period. During play and sports one should not become discouraged by wins or losses, but just enjoy for the sake of playing without allowing feelings of jealousy to enter in the mind and accepting that losing is a inevitable part of the game. Books, magazines, films etc. which are indecent should not be seen. Indecent pictures or photos should not be looked at or collected. One should abstain from seeing such corrupted and unproductive literature. One should read and attempt to understand daily at least 5 pages of a Pushti Marg or dharmic {religious} magazine or other publication. One should strictly abstain from maintaining relations with anyone who engages in the following: Opposes Pushti Marg; speaks or acts indecent criticizes Bhagavan, Guru, dharm; consumes forbidden foods; takes alcohol, drugs or a other addicting substance; abandons studies and wanders without purpose; engages in criminal acts; speaks disrespectfully to parent teachers or elders. One should never fear to be honest about one’s activities and should always admit the truth in all matters. Living in fear of telling the truth to be ruled out by the mind. If one has made any sort of mistake, big or small, one should go to the appropriate authority and confess. One should not have the mistakes overlooked, but, sh

t: MAIN PRINCIPLES TO BE KEPT IN MIND
x: Through one's gurudev, each vaishnav has surrendered every thing to Bhagwan and hence one's foremost duty is to perform His seva. It is an offence not to fulfill instructions of Gurudev. Therefore one should understand Shri Maha Prabhuji's principles in their real form and pray to him that we may attain the capacity to implement them in our lives. ANANYATA 'Ananyata' literally means 'not another'.Pushti Margiya Vaishnavs should keep exclusive 'ananya bhava' for Pushti Prabhu with no attachment to any other deity. Total devotion is said to be only when, through the heart, words and actions, all of one's thoughts, remembrance and words express stead fast exclusive ananya bhava. While walking, speaking, hearing, sleeping and with every breath all devotional feelings are expressed in one swarup alone. ASSOCIATION OR ACCOMPANIMENT Association is a matter of critical importance upon which one should ever remain highly cautious. If there is a association with a person who oppose Thakurji or Guru, one's own devotional sentiments will be destroyed and one will lose the way leading to the divine path. One should not have association with such persons so as to become entangled in worldly maya (illusions) but should associate with those who are perpetually absorbed in devotional expressions through whom Bhagavad bhava develops and deepens Prabhu transcends the mundane. Accordingly, satsang should at all times remain elevated. In comparison to 'Bhagavad ras' all other pleasures are of inferior quality. DISCREMINATION Shri Mahaprabhuji has given definite teachings for keeping Trust in Thakurji. The foremost sacred duty of a sevak is to have firm, unwavering trust in HIM. If one has lost faith in Prabhu, then devotion, seva and all actions are in vain. Devotions means to take full aashray in Prabhu, consider him to be the supreme and ultimate of all existence, live according to His wishes in all actions and face all circumstances, whatever they may be, with pleasure. Other than Prabhu, there is no power or capacity in the universe. He is the destroyer of suffering, the remover of adversity, the provider of all needs and He alone bestows protection. It is essential to have deep unwavering belief that Prabhu's will is the ultimate power and primordial cause in all of creation. ULTIMATE FAITH If one has firm belief in Prabhu, then only ultimate faith can develop. In all actions and interactions, while walking, moving, eating, drinking, standing and sitting, if one remembers that Prabhu is there at every moment, in every place with us, then, it can be said that ultimate faith has been established. With ultimate faith, there can never be greediness. One could overcome the grief. One will never worry, as to what will happen to him? A person with ultimate faith will be perpetually contented, fearless and unharmed in worldly and scriptural matters. 10 continued

For every Pushti soul, Ashtakshar Mantra is the ultimate and supreme mantra that is bestower of the highest attainments. Whenever anyone remembers and repeats 'ashtakshar mantra' deeply in the heart, he will experience supreme peace. Ashtakshar is not an ordinary mantra for obtaining mundane fruits but a supremely divine mantra bestowing the ultimate attainments. Each letter is embodied with divine powers and every vaishnav should repeat it unceasingly with a pure heart to attain those precious fruits. It destroys egotism, awakens the pure sentiments of 'das bhava', serving Prabhu as humble servant and bestows firm dedication to Prabhu's lotus feet. Ashtakshar mantra has not been created by anybody but it is wondrously and divinely manifested in 'Golok Dham'. THE DIVINE MANIFESTATION OF ASHTAKSHAR MANTRA Once Shri Thakurji and Shri Swaminiji, assumed the play of reciprocal maan-lila i.e. annoyance in love and emotions in their forest garden in Golok Dham, out of their own divine will, which got intensified to an extent beyond all limits. The beauty of Thakurji's hidden feminine aspect radiated on His lotus face, similarly the beauty of Swaminiji's hidden masculine aspect radiated on Hers. From the eternal union of these two hidden aspects, the burning fire of their passionate desire for reunion emerged in the shape of Shri Vallabh who witnessed the divine couple's entire lilas. “Soan-dhariya nij-hridhay-gha-tam pra-ka-ti-tum istri-good-bha-vat-ma-kam Pum rou-pam-ch: pu-nas-tah-dhantar-gatam pra-vi-visht sva-priye San-shi-lash-ta-vu-bha-yor-bha-bho ras-ma-yah krash-noh-hi-yet-sak-shi-kam Rou-pam-tate trit-yat-makam pram-bhi-de-ye-yam sadha vallabham” Shri Vallabh approached Swaminiji and with the utmost delicated sentiments of love escorted her into the presence of Thakurji. At the exalted moment of their ecstatic reunion, Shri Vallabh gazed towards them and pronounced, 'Shri Krishna Sharanam Mama', which means, 'Shri Swaminiji and Shri Krishna, I surrender to you' In this way 'Ashtakshar Mantra' got manifested. He, who is the reunited form of the divine couple, is exceedingly beloved to all the devotees of Golok Dham. Therefore, the name Shri Vallabh was given as; Vallabh means 'dearly beloved'. 11 continued Back to Ashtakshar Maha Mantra Page

Following this, according to Prabhu's instructions,Shri Maha Prabhuji manifested on earth to grant salvation to all daivi souls and to whom, he . bestowed ashtakshar mantra as the first initiation. This mantra has eight letters. 'ASHT' means eight and 'AKSHAR' means letter, thereby it is called, astakshar. These eight letters are not inanimate like ordinary letters, but, they are the bestower of wondrous divine powers. Each letter has profound depths of significance revealed by Shri Gosainji in his text 'description of the significance of Ashtakshar Mantra' . Initially let us consider the in-depth meaning of each individual letter in chronology. Attainment of good fortune and wealth Destroyer of sin Destroyer of the three types of sufferings Remover of the suffering of the cycle of birth and death. Attainment of divine knowledge Unwavering devotion for Shri Krishna Divine love for guru who reveals the supreme precious jewel,ShriKrishna. Merging with Shri Hari and being liberated from taking rebirth. Merging in the devotional path is superior to merger in the path of knowledge. 11.1 continued Back to Ashtakshar Maha Mantra Page

Now an in-depth elucidation of each of the letters. 'Shri' is the Bestower of good fortune. Here good fortune refers to a happy married life for which ample wealth is required. Wealth comes on its own to a devotee who unceasingly repeats ashtakshar mantra and he will not be required to engage in any efforts to obtain it himself. The reason for this is that Prabhu's devotees always are desire less, An apt example of this is in the account of Shri Maha Prabhuji's sevak Narayandas Brahmachari in which it is narrated that piles of money appeared in his home each night. Considering it to be impure dirt, he swept it out of the house in the morning and threw it away. From a worldly perspective, the pleasures of married life are considered to be the height of mundane pleasures and normally tremendous efforts are to be made to obtain them. One who ceaselessly repeats astakshar mantra, with no desire, will attain these pleasures just by the pronunciation of the letter 'Shri'. 'KRU' The pronounciation of this letter absolves a soul of the most heinous sins. All the means for becoming purified of sins delineated in the scriptures are rigorous and require undergoing much hardship and physical strain. Entrance into the devotional path becomes possible only when all sins have been destroyed. There are three types of sins (1) committed by the body, (2) committed through speech and (3) committed mentally. Unceasingly repeating ashtakshar mantra as suggested by Shri Mahaprabhuji is an exceedingly simple means for removing all of the three above mentioned sins and the pronounciation of the letter will destroy them all. 'SHNA' Human beings experience three types of sufferings (1) Adhibhautik (2) Adhyatmic and (3) Adhidaivik. On being relieved from these sufferings, the heart and mind becomes purified and then only Prabhu's seva and remembrance arises. Other than surrender, there is no means for purification. Pronunciation of this letter removes the three types of suffering, the heart and mind gets purified and pious inclination arises. ''SHA' By pronouncing this letter one is liberated from the cycle of birth and death and moving repeatedly through the eighty four lakhs of species. By becoming freed from egotism and attachment, one is released from worldly bondage and becomes worthy for bhagavad attainment. 11.2 continued Back to Ashtakshar Maha Mantra Page

”RA” One who is devoid of all worldly attachment, considers mundane pleasures to be insignificant. At that point an intense desire for attaining Prabhu arises and profound questioning begins. 'Who is Prabhu? What is His nature? What is the nature of an individual soul? How one can please Prabhu and thereby attain Him?' By pronouncing the letter, a penetrating requisitiveness on all these matters awakens and upon realization of this knowledge total fulfillment is attained. ”NAM” After realization of the knowledge about Prabhu's personality one attains Bhakti (Devotion) through a firm, unwavering love for Him. By pronunciation of the letter, the divine Love for HIM develops. Devotion is not attained by every one but depends upon divine grace. Prabhu bestows HIS graces on those to whom He so desires. Devotion' is superior of knowledge. ”MA” For entering into the path of devotion, guru's grace is mandatory and realization of Prabhu comes through the door of Guru. It is by guru's grace that one attains worthiness for seva. Guru is the bridge between Prabhu and the individual soul. Love for Prabhu comes where there is first love for guru. This love is attained by pronunciation of the letter. It is through Guru's grace that the darkness of ignorance is removed. Knowledge of Pusti Marg is attained and one experiences the 'anand' of Prabhu's own form. ”MA” Once the soul becomes totally and exclusively absorbed in Prabhu, by pronounciation of the letter, he merges with Prabhu and takes no further birth. In this way, each letter of ashtakshar mantra has the capacity to bestow divine powers. Knowing that the souls have surrendered to Him and are entirely devoid of any means for divine attainments, Shri Maha Prabhuji, in his unlimited compulsion bestowed this divine precious gift. To reveal the greatness of 'Ashtakshar Mantra' Shri Gusainji wrote the text 'Description of Ashtakshar Mantra' and by studying this in depth, one can understand its profound meaning. 11.3 continued Back to Ashtakshar Maha Mantra Page

“Shri Krishna-krishna-krishno-ti krishna-naam sadaha japeth, Aanan-dh: par-manan-dho vankuth: tasya nik-shi-tam.” Meaning: O Krishna. O Krishna. Whoever ceaselessly repeats the name of Krishna in this way attains the anand and paramanand of His divine form and attains His eternal abode of Golok Dham. “Sada: sma-re-tu yeh: Krishnam, ya-mas-tasya karo-ti kim, Bhas-mi bha-van-ti tasya-shu mahaa paa-tak naa-sha-ya .” Meaning: What harm can the Lord of Hell do to one who perpetually remembers Shri Krishna? By doing so, the most heinous of sins are destroyed. “Yah: sam-retu sadah mantra Shri Krishna sharan mama:, Ash-tak-sharam japo-nityam, yamo drasht-va hi shank-te.” Meaning: The Lord of Hell is afraid of one who unceasingly repeats ashtakshar mantra 'Shri Krishna Sharanam Mama.' “Shri man-trar-tha, praka-sh-yante ji-va-nam karya sadh-nah:, Ji-va-nam hit-kariar-arth guru Shri Vithalesh-va-rah:.” Meaning: By the power of ashtakshar mantra, liberation and other divine fruits may be attained .by daivi souls who are devoid of any means for these attainments. Guru Shri Vithalnathji (Sri Gosainji) is revealing his treatise on this subject. “Shri mu-khaat kath-yate sam-yak: sadash-tak-shar tat-tuva-tah:, Vi-vruti-hri-dayah yes-yah, so-yam Shri Vallab-ho bha-ve-tah.” Meaning: I myself am giving in- depth detailed commentary on the profound essence of ashtakshar mantra. One who has imbibed this and in whose heart ashtakshar mantra resides is a bhagavadiya beloved of Sri Vallabhacharyaji. 11.4 continued Back to Ashtakshar Maha Mantra Page

Shri – Shri so-baagh-ya sam-prap-ti, dhan-vaan, raj vallabh. Kra – shabd: shosh-yeth: paapam. Shnah – shabd:-sta-yah sum-hra-tim:. Sha - shabd:-ho nirdh:he-yo-nim. Ra – shabd:-do gi-yan ma-pru-yat. Nam – shabd-de-en sa-dah krish-noh:, dra-ta bhakti sadah bah-vet:. Ma – shabd-de-en gu-rou pree-ti, krishna rat-noh: pa-de-sha-ke. Ma – shab-deh: hari saa-yu-jai man-yah yo-nim na gach-chati. Meaning: By the pronounciation of this letter, the good fortune of wealth is attained. This letter destroys sin. All the three types of suffering is removed. From this letter one is liberated from the cycle of the birth and death. From this letter one attains the divine knowledge of Prabhu. This letter bestows unwavering and everlasting devotion for Shri Krishna. From this letter one attains love for Guru who imparts the teachings of Krishna's seva. From this letter one attains merger with Prabhu after which taking rebirth is not necessary. – Yeti Shri Krishna man-tra-arth, yo ja-pedh: vithale ratim, Bhakti vai-ra-giya-ma-prop-ti, buk-ti muk-ti kare sti-thay.” Meaning: By repeating ashtakshar mantra, with knowledge of its deeper significance, one attains love and devotion for Shri Krishna and detachment is attained. Pleasures and liberation are firmly established. “Sarverogopshamanam, sarva paapopnashnam, Riddhi shidhirgrahe shigrem vasthe sarvedha sathira. Meaning: From the repetition of ashtakshar mantra, one will be free. from illness and all sins will be destroyed. Wealth and power is immediately attained and one can reside in the home with security and stability. “Bhoot prath pishachadhi-viyagrah choradhi sankathe, Satravo mitrathamyanthi, sarp drasthvave mutthkha.” Meaning: One who recites ashtakshar mantra can not be harmed by ghosts or other spirits, wild animals, thieves, etc. and in adversities one is protected by Prabhu. In His shelter, enemies become friends and just as a mouse seeing a snake becomes frightened, enemies become filled with trepidation. “Krukiyah sarvristhani, kugraha sarvanashanha, Andhamurthi krishnoshiya hirdhey vasthe saadha.” Meaning: By repetition of ashtakshar mantra, sinful actions, harmful conditions, detrimental planetary configurations in one's horoscope are all destroyed and anand swarup Shri Krishna everlastingly resides in the heart. 11.5 continued Back to Ashtakshar Maha Mantra Page

“Thasayekutrapino dukham sukham sarvtra sarvadha, Aahooratram japennithyam, gurunammantramuttamam.” Meaning: The repetition of ashtakshar mantra removes all forms of suffering and happiness is attained in all spheres. This mantra is superior to all others and therefore it should be repeated unceasingly day and night. “Thamhi drasthvatriyo lokhah puthah sayu kimu maanvah, Madhiye ch sarvadha mantranam mantra rajothmottham.” Meaning: This mantra is the purifier of all the three worlds, so, what doubt can there be that it purifies the human soul? It is the king of all mantras and reigns supreme. “Edhmaveh paraykanth bhakthiman yah sadha samerath, Ridhi sidhi grah satiyam krishnthatpariya sundram. Bhakthanam hith kariyarth giyatviyam savjanotth ma.” Meaning: Anyone who perpetually repeats the mantra in solitude with reverence, attains wealth and powers. This mantra reveals the profound depths of Shri Krishna and Shri Maha Prabhuji has manifested it for the benefit of His devotees. “Vedhvakiya mahkaviyam purane bharathe ththa.” Meaning: This mantra is the essence of all scriptures,vedas, puranas etc. "Shrimadh vallab vakiyarth Shri Krishna Sharanam mama.” Meaning: The precious, invaluable words of Srimad Vallabhacharya Shri Krishna Sharanam Mama should be remembered perpetually. In this way to reveal the profound significance of ashtakshar mantra, Shri Gosainji has described each letter individually. 11.6 continued Back to Ashtakshar Maha Mantra Page

To impart his teachings that ashtakshar mantra should be repeated unceasingly, Shri Maha Prabhuji has written in the text Navratna: “Tasmatsarvhatmana nityam, Shri Krishna sharanam mama, Vaddbhirave sattham, sathymityav ma mathi.” Meaning: Shri Maha Prabhuji declares 'it is my view point that one should perpetually, with every bhava, repeat ashtakshar mantra and associate with those devotees who do so'. Shri Maha Prabhuji's main teaching is that ashtakshar mantra should be repeated with every bhava (Sarvatma Bhava) and unceasingly. Sri Gosaiji writes: “Yadhuktam thatcharano Shri Krishna sharanam mama, Aathah avasthi neschi-maihikay par lokikay.” Meaning: From the time of my father Shri Maha Prabhuji manifested Shri Krishna Sharanam Mama, we have been freed from all worries concerning any undertaking of this world or the transcendent sphere. In Shiksha Patra Shri Hariraiji states: “Aasmakam sadhanm sadiyam, Shri Krishan sharanam mama, Sampatsavapatsavepi sadha savachariyacharanodhitam.” Meaning: In favorable times and in adversity, 'Shri Krishna Sharanam Mama' manifested by Shri Mahaprabhuji, is both the means and the fruit. In this way many great scholars and Goswami Acharyas have described the profound significance of ashtakshar mantra, shedding light so that daivi souls may attain liberation. 11.7 continued Back to Ashtakshar Maha Mantra Page

One of the distinguishing characteristics of ashtakshar mantra is that it does not begin with Omkar, unlike other seed mantras which do begin with Omkar. According to scriptural law, any mantra begining with Omkar should not be pronounced in any impure state, such as, if one has been to the toilet and subsequently has not bathed or during the sutak etc. The prescribed method for purification must be adopted before such mantras are pronounced. In his unlimited compassion, Shri Maha Prabhuji bestowed graced upon daivi souls so that they would not be deprived of the right to repeat Prabhu's name even for an instant in this age of Kaliyuga. Perpetually, day and night under all circumstances, ashtakshar mantra should be repeated within the heart. Through this unceasing repetition, one can avoid useless thoughts and discussions and seva in the form of Prabhu's name can be performed because Prabhu's name has equal significance as Prabhu's seva in His own divine form as expressed in the following renown line from Sri Maha Prabhuji's writtings. “Roopnaam vibhadhan jagath kidhthi yo yeth.” Prabhu expresses His divine play in this universe through two means. His own form and His name. Also, as we walk and move about throughout the day and night, unknowingly, ants, beetles, and other insects are crushed beneath our feet. If at that moment Prabhu's name is being repeated in our heart, by the power of Bhagavad name, that soul will be liberated and we will be saved from the sin of killing a living soul. In this way by the repetition of ashtakshar mantra day and night with humbleness, all suffering and faults will be removed. Wealth, fame and other worldly pleasures will be gained and liberation, full absorption and merging into Prabhu's divine form will be realised. In the stories of Bhagwadiya, narrations on the ashtakshar mantra are found: One time as Shri Maha Prabhuji was moving in the circumambulation of Bharat he imparted the teaching Do not let even a moment pass without the repetition of ashtakshar mantra. Unceasingly pronouncing Shri Krishna Sharanam Mama'. Krishnadas Meghan did not fully realise the profound significance of this teaching. The group along with Shri Mahaprabhuji camp on the edge of a pond. For the purpose of making leaf plates and bowls, Krishnadas wandered quite distant into the dense forest. He came to a pond and on the water's edge a large parrot was sitting on the branch of a tree which had bent low. Being in the dark dense forest and seeing such strange parrot, which, he had never seen before, Krishnadas got frightened and began repeating ashtakshar mantra. He pronounced ashtakshar mantra three times and each time the parrot drank some water. Observing these strange, phenomena, which he had never seen before, Krishnadas hurriedly collected the leaves and returned back to the camp where Shri Maha Prabhuji inquired 'Krishnadas, what did you see in the forest?' Krishnadas related all that he had seen and experienced. To reveal the hidden reasons for the events, Shri Maha Prabhuji explained 'Krishnadas, that parrot which you saw is a devotee who has taken birth as a bird. He practice unceasingly repetition of ashtakshar mantra. Hearing you reciting it three times, he was able to pause for a moment to quench his thirst. I have explained to all of you formerly that the perpetual repetition of ashtakshar mantra is for your welfare and the welfare of those who will hear it". In this way Shri Maha Prabhuji taught the power of ashtakshar mantra to his intimate sevaks. In the treatise called Narad Panchratra, the greatness of ashtakshar mantra is described. By reciting ashtakshar mantra, sinful actions, adverse circumstances and the devastation of unfavorable planetary configuration are all removed and the anand swarup Shri Krishna everlastingly resides in the heart. If the moment or crisis or disaster arises, on remembering ashtakshar mantra deeply in the heart, the difficulties will be resolved of its own and by the grac

Not only in Pushti Marg but unversally in Sanatan Dharm, vedas and scriptures, Gurudev is given a place of distinction. 'GU' means darkness and 'RU' means remover. Human life is pervaded with darkness. With Guru's radiant light of knowledge that darkness is removed and life becomes filled with illumination. It is because of that darkness that the eyes remains closed, and are unable to have Bhagavad darshan. A devotee is incapable of independently knowing and seeing even that which is most close. There are those who acquire book knowledge and consider it to be the ultimate but in reality the final goal is Bhagwan’s realization and without guru's grace that can never be achieved. To attain any goal in the life, it is necessary to abandon egotistic actions and to surrender, because it is only through the power of guru's unbound grace that in this kaliyuga any soul pervaded irretrievably with imperfections can become detached from the worldly ocean and move towards Bhagavad attainment. It is said that the position of guru in one's life surpasses even that of Bhagavan himself because, it is through gurudev that Bhagavan is attained. The great bhakta Kabirji's reknown verse says: “Guru govind dhono khade kinko lagu pai? Balihari gurudevki govind diyo dhikay.” If we do not find guru, there is no one who can take us to Prabhu. Once Shri Maha Prabhuji was sleeping with his head resting in Damodardas Hasaniji's lap near Sunder Shila on the sacred ground at the base of Girirjji at Jatipura. At that moment. Shri Nathji came there. Damodasdasji gestured with his hand to stop HIM so as not to awaken Shri Maha Prabhuji due to the sound of his ankle bracelets. On awakening, when this became known to Sri Maha Prabhuji, he asked Damodasdasji', what have you done?' Damodardasji replied, 'What is bigger, the gift or the giver of the gift'. 'Maharaj, who has revealed Shri Nathji to me? It is by your grace that I have come to know Him.' The precious endowment is Shri Nathji and the giver is Shri Maha Prabhuji, that is, it is by Shri Mahaprabhuji's grace that Shri Nathji is attained. Accordingly, the guru holds the ultimate position of supremacy in human life and surpasses all as worthy of worship. In Vedas, Puranas and other scriptures it is emphasised that guru and Bhagvan are not to be differentiated. The great gyani Pritamdasji writes: “Vani sake ne varnvi sadhguru kerum savroopam. Maan budhi pauche nahi upma sahith sanup, Guru padh pankaj pujtam re chodhalokay pujaye, Shiv viranchi ne shardha gurunam jaas gaya.” It is written in Srimad Bhagavat that a devotee, devotion, guru and Bhagvan are spoken of as four seperate entities but in fact they are one only. 12 continued

For those who take birth, death is inevitable. If there is any bitter truth in the life, it is death and fear of death is felt universally by all human beings. As disease can be the cause of death, constant efforts should be made to avoid it by implementing the appropriate treatment. Persistent striving should be made to eliminate any conditions which may cause sudden death. Solutions should be sought with determination to prevent untimely death at an early age. Support of the different fields of knowledge should be taken, such as dharm, science, astrology, religion, etc. It is a matter of great surprise that people walk knowingly on the path of addiction and willingly embrace death. For many eras, man has formed habit of partaking of addicting substances like alcohol, palm tree juice, cocaine, heroin, hash, marjuana, tobacco etc. finding some excuses or the other, viz.. Ignorance, submitting to social pressure etc and ultimately embrace their own death and at the same time, cause destruction of their family, society, country and entire world. Generally, people become addicted before they realise the extent of the danger. Children, teenagers and young adults become addicted to bidi, pan masala, charas, hashish, alcohol etc. and consequently the flower. of their youth withers and a multitude of physical and mental illnesses develops, such as weakness, cough, asthama, T.B., Cancer, constipation, indigestion, sleeplessness, joint pains, AIDS, mental instability and mental weakness. Addiction at an early age leads to loss of physical and mental capacity, debilitating the person rendering him incapable of stability or discipline. Such incompetence, indiscipline, irresponsibility and extravagant spending precipitate failure in business, service, career and other types of employment. In married life, alcohol and other addictions cause divorce, disputes and inability to adjust. In such a conflict-ridden environment, children are prevented from progressing normally and often fall in their father's foot steps, falling victim them elves to addiction. With the increase of addiction, begging, poverty, disease, indiscipline, irresponsibility, incompetence, illiteracy, self-interest, wasteful spending, crimes, terrorism etc. are all on the rise. These factors retard the progress of the country and under such conditions, providing security and protection to the public has become a critical problem. Throughout history, Governments, Institutions and dedicated individuals, all over the world, have implemented countless programmes, to prohibit addiction but, if information would be presented to school going children by institutions devoted to protecting the traditional values of the society, conveying the frightening consequences of addiction, there could be substantial progress in this direction. Of all the types of addictions, alcohol and tobacco consumption are most prevalent and therefore should be understood in depth. 13

Human beings are trapped in doubt arising from a wide range of factors and experience constant mental tension. Instead of searching for an appropriate solution to alleviate this, alcohol consumption is opted for as a shortcut relief. Experiencing such tension due to insecurity or a feeling of being exploited, people turn to alcohol for support and then fall victim to addiction. Countless people feel weak and incapable and become addicted to alcohol to alleviate the sense of shame arising from this. In many families, alcohol is consumed in the home. Undesirable association from business contacts and activities in society, where there is social pressure to drink, leads to addiction. Effects of alcohol consumption: .......Alcohol conumption damags the tissues of the face. When alcohol is taken into the stomach, a small portion enters the blood stream and the remainder enters the small intestines. Once alcohol enters the blood stream, it causes damages to all tissues throughout the body. Serious harm is done to the digestive system. .......Alcohol consumption causes memory loss, particularly, during the period of intoxication. When there is often a total lapse of memory, giving rise to a wide range of tensions. Alcohol addiction causes irritability and a feeling of isolation. .......According to one scientific study, it was established that there is not a single part of the body which is not damaged from alcohol consumption. .......Alcohol consumption causes cirrtiosis of the liver which is a fatal disease and also creates the possibility of heart disease. The digestive tract and stomach are damaged, ulcers develops and the possibility of stomach cancer arises. In addition to that, brain cells are severally damaged and the entire nervous and skeletal system is weakened. .......The most critical side-effect of alcohol consumption is caused to the brain. Brain activity is debilitated and the nervous system network carrying brain messages is disturbed, accompanied by personality break down with symptoms of excessive talkativeness, short-temper, argumentativeness and violence. Mental balance is lost and the judgment and decision making faculty is critically disturbed. .......Alcohol consumption causes serious damage to the activity of the liver and kidney resulting in swelling of the body, water retention in the stomach, vomiting blood and ultimately escorting the person in the direction of death. In addition to this, heart activity is slowed, consequently, disturbing the flow of blood in the blood vessel system causing high blood pressure. The consumption of alcohol greatly increases the possibility of falling victim to accident. It is a threatening evil and invitation to self-destruction. 14 continued

”Cigarette smoking is injurious to health' To smoke cigarettes after seeing this critical warning is to walk knowingly in the direction of one's own death. It can be understood if some thing dangerous is done out of ignorance but, to have full knowledge and still disregard judgments to one's benefit and engage in self destructive actions, is to invite inevitable suffering. In any case, even in ignorance, dangerous cancer producing poisonous chemicals enter lungs by smoking. Cigarettes contain nicotine, a highly harmful substance with a damaging effect to the entire nervous system. To smoke is to knowingly allow this danger to directly enter the brain. According to the scientific studies, dangers of cigarette smoking are as follows: .....Cigarette smoking causes decrease of life expectancy. .....Cigarette smoking causes death due to fatal side-effects. .....Cigarette smoking is an invitation to cancer. Cigarette smoking causes death due to heart disease. .....Cigarette smoking increases the chances of death due to stomach ulcer. .....Cigarette smoking in pregnancy causes damages to the unborn fetus. It can cause premature birth and stillbirth. .....Cigarette smoking causes irregular blood pressure. .....Cigarette smoking causes hardening of the arteries and thinning of the blood vessels obstructing the flow of blood. It is the invitation to heart disease. .....Cigarette smoking causes a wide range of lung diseases such as chronic bronchitis, emphysema, cough, shrinking of the breathing passages causing breathing difficulties and swelling in the lungs. Insufficient intake of oxygen causes heavy strain on the lungs. .....Cigarette smoking causes ulcers in the stomach and small intestines inducing vomiting and danger of death. .....Cigarette smoking causes the production of cyanides which has strong adverse effect on the eyes, impairing vision and possibly to blindness. Cigarette smoking and chewing tobacco causes throat and mouth cancer. .....Cigarette smoking damages salivary glands in the mouth. Saliva decreases, the mouth becomes dry and digestive capacity weakens. Chemical particles contained in the smoke accumulate between the teeth and in the throat which can cause cancer or other non malignant tumors. The teeth become weak and the sense of taste and smell is impaired. .....Cigarette smoking causes adverse effects to all organs of the body and gives birth to countless diseases and inevitable unbearable suffering. Cigarette smoking is a waste of time and money. The amount of rupees spent uselessly and the loss of working hours is so incredibly high that it is beyond the imagination. According to one survey, annually throughout the entire world, 3,000 Arab rupees go up in cigarette smoking and an estimated 24,000 Arab rupees is spent on advertising. If this amount of money is spent of human development what could not be accomplished? It is unimaginable. According to a survey conducted in 1964 in a single year a total of 30, 60,000 man hours were lost due to the side-effects of smoking. 15 continued

The eleventh day of the moon during the month of Shravan is observed as 'Pavitra Ekadisi'. It is the inception of Pushti Marg and on that auspicious day, vaishnavs offer a pavitra to Shri Thakurji. The following day, 'Pavitra Baras' is the twelfth day of the new moon and on that day, Goswami Acharyas place a pavitra around each other's necks, feed misri to each other and without giving any thought as to who is elder or younger, touch each other's feet and do dandvat. Following this all vaishnavs place a pavitra around their Guru's neck, feed them misri and experience this to be the ultimate good fortune. UNDERSTANDING PAVITRA BHAVANA In the year 1549, third day of the new moon in the month of Sravan, Srimad Vallabhacharya Mahaprabhuji began a one week discourse on Srimad Bhagavat and completed it on the night of the eleventh day. That night in Gokul, on Govindghat, Shri Mahaprabhuji was deeply immersed in thought, 'During the age of Kaliyuga souls are pervaded with imperfections. In what manner can they be freed entirely from these faults and realise Bhagavad swarup?'. The sacred spot of this momentous event was Govindghat. 'GO' means sense organs, 'VIND' means attain and 'GHAT' means beautiful form. Souls are pervaded with fault. When all their sense organs are transformed into a divine form then only Prabhu will accept their seva. As Shri Mahaprabhuji was pondering in this way at midnight, Shri Thakurji manifested and decreed that any soul who would take 'Brahm sambandh' from Shri Mahaprabhuji would become freed of all faults and HE would accept them. Following this, Shri Mahaprabhuji sang Madhurashtak Stotra and placed a 360 cotton thread pavitra around Shri Thakurji's neck and fed him misri. The eleventh day of Shravan is called Putrada (giver of sons) Ekadisi. Shri Acharyaji worships with balbhava and therefore ShriNathji manifested at mid night with the balbhava swarup of Shri Gokulchandramaji. The presiding devta for the month of Shravan is Bhagvan Vishnu Himself and therefore it is highly sacred. It is said that this month facilitated Bhagavad attainment. During ascension each day the moon's power and radiance increases dispelling darkness, freeing daivi souls of their adhibhautik faults. On the eleventh day upvas (fast) is kept. 'UP' means near and 'VAS' means reside. One is freed from worldly activities and resides in Prabhu's presence. On that day the five sense organs of action, the five sense organs of knowledge and the mind, totaling eleven are all applied and utilised in seva, thus the name 'upvas' is given in which the adhyatmic faults of daivi souls are 'removed. For the salvation of 'nisadhan' daivi souls (i.e. souls without any means or practice for salvation) Saraswat Kalp, Prabhu manifested at midnight on the eleventh day of shravan to bestow upon these souls Brahmsambandh through Shri Mahaprabhuji for removing all adhidaivic faults. 16 continued

Puran Purushottam Prabhu Shri Krishna is an ocean of 16 divine qualities. His lilas span the 6 seasons. 16 multiplied by 6 is 96. If this is multiplied by 3, representing the three types of devotees, rajas, tamas and satvik, it reaches the sum of 288. Adding to that, the 12 months, one reaches 300. By adding the 60 minutes of an hour a total of 360 is obtained and therefore a 360 thread cotton pavitra is offered to Prabhu. One year has 360 days. After taking Brahm Sambandh each vaishnav should perform seva daily offering new clothes and food preparations to Thakurji. However, human beings have limited capacity and are unable to fulfill this in totality. Therefore, by offering a 360 thread pavitra, the clothing seva of an entire year is represented. Prabhu is compassionate and bestows His grace by accepting this as a full year's seva. WHY IS A COTTON PAVITRA CALLED 'PAVITRA' (SACRED) That which is most beloved to us, the most pure and sacred, should be offered to Prabhu. Cotton is considered to be the most beautiful, pure and sacred and therefore is utilized in all vedic rituals. Of all things, cotton is the most quickly consumed by fire and for these reasons is considered to be sacred. Shri Hariraiji wrote a treatise entitled 'PA VITRAMANDAN'. In a 360 thread cotton pavitra 108 knots are tied just as there are 108 knots in a mankamala (Japmala) through which, Bhagavad bhajan and bhava is perfected. In a couplet from the scriptures: Kruthe lashamtu varshanitrathayamyutam ththa Dhuvapure thu sastrani kaloo varshratam samrutam These words express that in Satyuga, life spans one lakh years, in Tretayuga ten thousand years, Dwaparyuga one thousand years and in Kaliyuga life span is not subject to any rules. One can be freed of one destined span and obtain pleasure even in a moment, by the repetition of Bhagvad name one hundred times is sufficient to absolve one of their faults. According to Shri Mahaprabhuji's instructions, four kinds of pavitras are prepared and offered, each with its own individual bhava. Kesri, Champa, yellow-satvik, predominant Swaminiji, Radhaji's bhava red, pink-rajas, Chandrvaliji's bhava green-tamas, Radha sahacheri, kumarika's bhava blue, purple-nirguna, Yamunaji's bhava. The great Ashtasakha poet and Bhagvad bhakta Paramananddasji describes pavitra: Paitra peharth rajkumar Thinulok pavitra kiya hai shri vithalgirdhar Aathi hi pavitra priya bahu bileshAt Nirkhat bhavan bhayo bhar Parmanand pavitra kimala Gokul ki brajnari. 16.1 continued

'Kankarwad' a village in the 'Talang District' situated on the southern banks of 'River Krishna', in the vicinity of 'Mount Vyo-mas-thamba' in what is presently known as 'Andhra Pradesh' in 'India' there lived a 'YAJURVEDI', THIRTY THIRD in line, BHARAT-DWAJ GOTRA, one TALANG BRAHMIN named SHRI NARAYAN DIXIT also known as SHRI YAGNANARAYAN BHATT (KAMBHAMPATY). He was Shri Ved Avtaar. He was a very great scholar he had memorised all The Four Vedas and Six Shas-tras. Many rajas & rich people were his students. He being ardent devotee of Shri Baghwan Krishna, saw a auspicious moment and performed SOM YAGYA. He kept on performing SOM YAGYA'S till he reached 32nd SOM YAGYA, at that moment a voice was heard from the KUND altar “Narayan Bhatt you are very fortunate PURNAH: PUR-SHO-TAM has accepted your SOM YAGYA'S therefore PURNA PRUSOTAM SHRI KRISHNA will be born in your family when 100th SOM YAGYA will be completed within your family. At the sametime SHRI MADAN MOHANJI appeared from the altar [AGNI KUND]. This is One of the seven SAWROOPS. SHRI MADAN MOHANJI'S Haveli is in KAMVAN-VIRAJ. Lots of people praised SHRI NARAYAN DIXIT. He taught VED to thousand of PANDITS, but few disbelivers said what is great in teaching VED to human being , can he teach Ved to this buffalo. On hearing this he took stick and touched the buffalo and buffalo started to recited the Vedic Hymns. His son GANGADHAR BHATT or GANGADHAR DIXIT was also great scholar, he use to offer everyday food to Brahmins give Dhan (Money) to them. He performed twenty 28 SOM YAGYA'S. His fame spread and people used to call him as SHRI SHIVJI’S Avtaar. One of the pandits told him SHIV had GANGAJI IN HIS HAIR, so GANGADHARJI untied his hair the GANGAJI started flowing from his hairs. His son, GANPATI DIXIT also known as GANAPATI BHATT who performed 30 SOM YAGA'S. He taught thousands of people, so people praised him and called him as GANPATI’S Avtaar. But one of them told I will believe only if he rain rats. On hearing so he rained rats around 16 miles diameter for period 3 hours. 45 minutes. This gave him a lot of fame. His son VALLAB DIXIT also known as VALLABH BHATT who was glorious. He performed 5 SOM YAGYA'S. He was known as SURIYA NARAYAN’S Avtaar. But few of them against him said if he is SURIYA NARYAN’S Avtaar then we want to see SUN SHINE in the middle of the night. He did midday, in 12 kos area, at midnight!!!. His son LAXMAN BHATT (SHRI VASUDEV’S Avtaar) performed 5 SOMYAGYA and thus 100th yagya was performed and he heard from the sky that PURNA PURSOTAM will be born . SHRI NARAYAN DIXIT also known as SHRI YAGNANARAYAN BHATT 32 SOM-YAGYA His son SHRI GANGADHAR DIXIT also known as SHRI GANGADHAR BHATT 27 SOM-YAGYA His son SHRI GANPATHI DIXIT also known as SHRI GANPATHI BHATT 32 SOM-YAGYA His son SHRI VALLAB DIXIT also known as SHRI VALLAB BHATT 5 SOM-YAGYA His son SHRI LAXMAN DIXIT also known as SHRI LAXMAN BHATT 5 SOM-YAGYA he is the father of JAGAT GURU SHRI MADH VALLABHACHARYA. 3

Shri laxman dixit finally finished 100th SOM-YAG-YA and he decided to offer sanctified food [Prasad] as meal to 125,000 Brahmins. He took his family to Holy City of KASHI for YATRA, on this way he stopped at another Holy City of PRA-YAG for THIRTH-YATRA and then he moved to KASHI again. At HANUMAN-GHAT he rented a house and stayed there. Time elasped and one fine day he heard a muslim ruler is coming here to attack, due to this he left KASHI for his home town in the south. The whole journey was on foot, tiring and troublesome. After leaving KASHI he came to CHAMPA-RAN, where his eighth month pregnant wife SHRI IIL-LAMA-GARU-JI had some problem due to tiring journey. She had to abort her child pre-suming lifeless, that was the eleventh (11TH) day of the dark half of the Chaitra Krishna Ekadashi of Vikram Samvat 1535, (1475 AD) she tore the part of her sari and wraped the child and kept under the SHAMI-VRAKSH (located in the middle of dense jungle of CHAMPA-RAN, well known for its wild animals) and covered it with dry leaves. In grief they came out of the jungle, and went a little far where they stayed. At night when they slept, BAGHWAN appeared in their dream, His divine words were “I ,AS CHILD HAVE INCARNATED AND YOU HAVE LEFT ME IN CHAMPA-RAN JUNGLE, COME AND FETCH ME”. This dream made them awake in joy. Hurriedly, they rushed to the spot where they had left their beloved son. On arriving there, to their surprise they found a {”FIRE BURNING IN A CIRCLE OF 20 YARDS RADIUS. WHAT AN AMAZING SCENE!!! THE TREES WERE AT THEIR FULLEST GREEN, THE FLOWERS BLOSSOMED, THE FRUITS WERE HEAVY FULL OF JUICE, RIPPENED TO FALL, THE FLOWERS WERE SHOWERING. THE SHAMI-VRAKSH HAD A PRIVILEDGE TO SHELTER PURNA: PUR-SHOTAM. THE CHILD WAS PLAYING, ENJOYING THE FRESH AIR, SUCKING THE THUMB OF HIS TOE, LOOKING AT COLOURFULL TREES, THE RAYS OF RISING SUN. THE WINDS WERE MILDLY BLOWING CARING THE FRAGRANCE OF VARIOUS FLOWERS. THE CLOUDS HAVE GATHERED, IT STARTED TO DRIZZLE. THE RIVERS THAT WERE OVER FLOWING STOPPED FLOODING. THERE WAS PIN DROP SILENT. THE LION AND TIGER HAD NOT ONLY FORGOTTEN TO ROAR BUT THEY SAT BESIDE THE COWS AND DEER. THE BIRDS HAD STOPPED FLYING, INSTEAD THEY GATHERED ON TOP OF TREES. NOBODY CAN EVER DREAM SUCH A SCENARIO!!!! THE WHOLE SURRONDINGS BECAME EXOTIC. THE ENTIRE CELESTIAL SPHERE WAS ENGULFED WITH SAT-VIK GUN. SHRI LAXMAN DIXIT TOLD TO SHRI IIL-LAMA-GARU-JI IF HE IS YOUR SON THEN THE FIRE WILL GIVE YOU THE WAY, AND SO DID, IT HAPPENED SHE WENT INSIDE THE FIRE CIRCLE (THAT HAD ENGULFED THE BABY AS PROTECTIVE SHIELD ) AND HURRIEDLY SHE PICKED HER SON, HERE THERE ARE NO WORDS TO EXPRESS EXECPT MOTHERLY LOVE”}. ON THE OTHER SIDE WERE ALL THE SAINTS AND SAGES THE RISHI, MUNIS, BELOVED BAKTH'S WHO LIKE A FLOCK OF BIRDS HAD GATHERED TO HAVE A GLIMPSE OF THEIR BELOVED BABY (WHO WAS NAMED VALLABH) FOR WHOM THEY HAVE WAITED FOR YEARS. TODAY IS THE DAY FOR WHOM DEVIS, DEV-TAS EVEN BRAHMA AND SHIV WANTED TO HAVE DHAR-SHAN. THEY ALL ON THEIR CHARIOT CAME AND STOPPED IN MID AIR AND STARTED SHOWERING FLOWERS, THE GHAN-DAR-VAS WERE DANCING. THE ATMOSPHERE WAS SO PLEASANT THAT IT ENCOURAGED PEOPLE TO DANCE. ON THE OTHER HAND SHRI IIL-LAMA-GARU-JI BROUGHT HER BELOVED SON TO SHRI LAXMAN DIXIT-JI WHO WAS SO MUCH MOVED THAT HE VOWED TO GIVE AWAY 100,000 COWS TO BRAHMINS. HE TOOK OUT THE UPRANA AND TULSI KANTHI MALA WHICH HE HAD RECEIVED FROM SHRI THAKUR-JI DURING HIS DREAM HE WRAPPED THE CHILD IN UPRANA WORE THE TULSI MALA. THERE ARE NO WORDS TO EXPRESS THE BEAUTY OF THE CHILD. FROM NEARBY WELL CAME OUT SHRI NAND-BAWA, SHRI YASO-DHA-JI, SHRI ROHINI-JI, SHRI VRASH-BAN-JI, SHRI KIRTI-JI AND ALL THE CHAMPA-RAN FOREST TURNED INTO VRAJ. SHRI NAND-BAWA PERFORMED THE ABI-SHEK OF SHRI LAXMAN BHATTJI. THE WHOLE SOIL OF CHAMPARAN WAS FULL OF MILK, BUTTER AND DHAI. THE WHOLE OF CHAMPA-RAN HAD BEEN TURNED TO VRAJ. THE GOPS AND GOPIS HAS ASSEMBLED AND NAND-MAHO-UTSAV HAS JUST BEGAN. {|| NAND GHE-R ANAND BHA-YOH JAI KANI-YAH LAL KI || || HATHI-DIYOH, GORAH

t: Alokik (divine) power of "Shri Aacha-riya-charan Shri Madh-Vallabh-acha-riya-ji"
x: Understanding the Alokik (divine) power of "Shri Aacha-riya-charan Shri Madh-Vallabh-acha-riya-ji", the GURU, of Pustimargiya Vaishnav's. Name: Shri Vallabh Dev Name: Shri Krishna-prasadh Month's Name: Shri Janardhan Nak-sha-tra Name: Shra-visht Born On: Chaitra Vadh 11., v.s.1535., Sa-ke 1400 (1479 AD), Sunday at Noon (12pm.) Purvabhadra Padh: Gha-nishta Nakshatra, Mash Sankranthi, Vras-chik Lagna. Place of Birth: Champaran, near Raipur., Madras. Father's Name: Shri Laxman Bhatt. Mother's Name: Shri Ill-lamagaru. Naming Ceremony: This ceremony was performed on the 11th day from the birth according to Vedic rites. He was named as "VALLABH". Five Tatvas (essences) of life : These five tatvas has shown the importance of BRAJBOOMI. Prathvi Tatva: (Earth) Shri Yamunaji's acceptance. Jal Tatva: (Water) To show Shri Krishna's Lilas. Tej Tatva: (Light) To accept Shri Gowardhan as Haridas and Shrinathji as one. Vayu Tatva: (Air) To give Rus-dhaan and to show Shri Krishna's Ras-lila. Akas Tatva: (Space) To produce the clear meaning of His Granth (books). Three Gunas: Satvik Gun (Truth,Piousness), Rajasik (Intermediate between occasional Satvik and moderate Lie), Tamasik (Always Demoniac and occasional Rajasik). In the same way:- Aadi-bho-tic (Material) as Human Form, Aadi-de-vic (Krishna-maye) and Aadi-yat-mic (Divinly) Shri Vallabh Swaroop. Why Birth in Vaishak Maas (Month)? Let's read what Vedic Scriptures have to say about this Month "Madhav seet Vasake Maasi tanyo Madusudan Vallabay"(from Saknd pruan)means being lovable Vasake month Madhusudan has accepted Shri Vallabh's swaroop. || Padmah Pruan: || "Masoo Vaisake naamoo mai priyo vai madhughateenh" "Sarvaschathithayo Madhya madhavaikadasipriyai" || Brahma Puran: || "Yatha tai madhavo maso Vallabho Madhusudnah". The essence of Vaisak Maas has four important points: Bhagwan loves this Vaisak Month. Preat-duwar's stories. Tulsi's dhal, pujan and ka-tha(story) & Dha-an (Offerings, Donation): Umbrella, Paduka (wooden sandal) Jal (water) Panka (hand fan) and Shrad Shri Vallabh's Avataar in this month transformed the above four points into Divie four: Bhagwan loves this Vaisak Maas: Shri Vallabh gave tremendous happiness of Seva to the house where He established Shri Thakuji's Swaroop. Preat-duwar: Without Bhagwan's Seva we all human being are preat (dead body). He freed those people. Importance of Tulsi: To surrender through Tulsi leaves and to wear Tulsi's Kanti (neck wear). Importance of Dha-an: To offer every thing to Shri Thakuji and than to distribute as prasad to vaishanvas. 4.1

t: Highlights of some of Important events of Shri Vallabh's life
x: Understanding the Alokik (divine) power of "Shri Aacha-riya-charan Shri Madh-Vallabh-acha-riya-ji", the GURU, of Pustimargiya Vaishnav's. You established six Lilas on the Earth: Your Aavtaar on the earth is to pardon Devi Jeva's (Divine Souls) of its sins, to establish (jeva's) relation wth Bhagwan and to enjoy the Lila Darshan. Based on Shri-Madh-Bhagwat-ji You showed the way in Subodh-ni-ji's, Tika (an extended and descriptively elaborate work on Shri Madh-Baghwad). You defeated Maya-vaad (Material Illusion) and established Nishkam Bhakti Margh (Path of Selfless Devotion). Three times You had Prithvi Pradh-shina and by this way You accepted Satvik, Rajasik and Tamasik Bhakth. Through Pusti Margh You showed the strength Lovable Seva and accepted Stree (Female) and Shudra's. Aa-achariya's, Sevak's, and learned people of those time were shown miracles and made them believe in Pusti Marg. Highlights of some of Important events of Shri Vallabh's life. Year wise Divine Profile: ||1535 || Pra-gha-tiya Ustav (Time of Avtaar) where You showed:-- Your Agni Swaroop. You are Shri Krishna himself by creating Ratna Jarit Mahal (Nandalay-Palace made of Precious Stones) where in Jan-mash-tami Maha Ustav was celebrated with all the Gop's and Gopi's, Nand-baba & Jaso-da Maiya herself along with Vrash-bhan-ji & Kirti-ji. ||1545 || Sash-trat in Jagdish-raj's sabha where in You were the winner. ||1546 || Sash-trat with Ghat Sarsvati in Ujjain in Viduth's sabha and you defeated him and freed Sarsvati-ji. ||1548 || Vidya-nagar Viduth's sabha where in you had Sash-trat with opponents and was victorious. ||1549 || Elaborate Sash-trat in Kashi with Dundhi-raj Yogi. ||1550 || At midnight on Thakurani Ghat Shri Goverdhan-dharan Shri-Nathji appeared and explained to Him about Brahma-samband Diksha. ||1553 || Shri Vallabh performed first Prithivi Parikrama. ||1556 || At Mount Shri Goverdhan He did Stha-pana of Shri-Nathji's Swaroop, and established Shri-Nathji's Seva. ||1558 || Shri Vallabh performed second Prithivi Parikrama. ||1558 || Shri Vallabh got married with Divine Shri Maha-Laxmi-Ji, the daughter of Shri Madumangal ||1558 || In Kashi Sash-trat through Patra-valam-ban and was victorious. ||1565 || Sash-trat in Vidya-nagar in the sabha of Krishna-dev Raja and was honored with a letter declaring Him as victorious. At the same time the king honored Him with Kanka-abhishek (a bath with gold coins). Shri Vallabh did not accept those coins & told king to distribute it to Brahmins. ||1566 || Shri Vallabh performed third Prithivi Parikrama. ||1566 || Shri Vallabh took Shri Maha-Laxmi-ji to Adel, Your home town. ||1567 || In Ashwin Krishna 12 ,Your first son, Shri Gopi-nath-ji was born. ||1572 || In Posh Krishna 9, Your second son Shri Vithal-nath-ji was born. ||1587 || You had taken a vow of total Silence and Brahma-chari for Fourty Days. ||1587 || In Aashad Shukla 3 at mid-day you entered Shri Ganga-ji and disappeared with a ball of fire which arose from Gangaji when You entered in it. This ball of fire disappeared in the sky. Grantha's (Books) written by Him: You have written lots of Granthas in shot a Sagar (ocean), but most important are 84, few of them are Sodas-Granth (Sixteen Books), Shri Subodh-niji (based on Shri Madh Bhagwat-ji).> His Sevaks: You have un-accountable Sevaks it includes everybody living and non-living beings, but the most important are 84 Vaishnavas, they in other words are the pillars of Pusti Margh. Prithivi Parikramas: During Your three Prithivi Parikramas You traveled across the entire Bharat Varsh, but 84 places are most important where You recited Shri-Madh-Bhagwat. These places are known as 84 Bathakji's. Your Pratis-tha-pit and Seviya Swaroops: There are more than 51 different Swaroops: Shri Bal-Krishna-lal {20} Shri Madan Mohan-ji {10} Shri Navneet-priya-ji {4} Shri Mathuresh-ji {3} Shri Vithal-nath-ji Shri Dwarka-nath-ji Shri Gokal-nath-ji Shri Chandra-ma-ji Shri Aasht-bhu-ja-ji Shri Dhamodhar-ji Shri Kaliyan-rai-ji Shr

SHRI HARI-RAI-JI was born in Sri-madh Gokul on Ashwin vad 5th sam-vant 1647. SHRI HARI-RAI-JI is the son of Shri Kaliyan-rai-ji, who in turn is the son of Shri Govind-rai-ji, who is second son of Shri Vithal-nath-ji (Gusain-ji). I am sure there will not be any vaishnav who do not know Shri Gusain-ji, He is son of SHRI VALLABH, i.e., SHRI MADH VALLABH. He is great great grand father of SHRI HARI-RAI-JI. SHRI HARI-RAI-JI is handsome, elegant, an artist of high quality, a unique scholar with highest knowledge of literature. He inheritated all traits from SHRI VALLABH-ACHA-RAYA, a true love and affection for SHRI GOVARDHAN-DHA-RAN SHRI-NATH-JI. He willingly surrendered everything to him and is always ready to serve SHRI-NATH-JI. Being SAT-VIK SWAROOP of SHRI MAHA-PRABHU-JI, He is known as SHRI HARI-RAI-MAHA-PRA-BHU-JI. He is the author of SHRI-NATH-JI'S pra-ga-tiya varta. For all VAISHNA'S he has written 166 books in Sanskrit, 30 in Vraj-bha-sha and most important are 41 letters he wrote to His younger brother SHRI GO-PESH-WAR-JI. These letters are known as SHIK-SHA-PATRA. He compiled 40 pads on SHRI YAMUNA-JI. He (his material life visible to all- vaishnav and ordinary people alike) lived 125 years, and still living among us through His books for the ordinary eye, but for alo-kik vaishnav the entire SHRI VALLABH KUL is immortal. SHRI GOKAL-NATH-JI, the second son of SHRI VITHAL-NATH-JI, graced SHRI HARI-RAI-JI by giving BRA-MAH-SAM-BANDH. He treated GURU, VAISHNAV & THAKURJI (SHRI NATHJI) as one. KEEP IN MIND TO READ DAILY “SHIK-SHA-PATRA” 5

Achariyacharan Shrimadh Vallabhachariyaji He is the son of Shri Laxmanbutt and Shri Illamagaru , who completed 100th Somyagiya Born in Vashak krishnapacx 11th 1535 in Champaran. Gotra- Bharatdwagh, Ved – Krishna yajurved. Shakha – Taitri He accepted the allokik five tatevas of Brijbumi, i.e. Pruthivitatva is Shri Yamunaji which flows in Brijbumi. Jaltatva is Purna Prusotam Nand Kumar Shri Krishna’s Lila, performed in Brijbumi. Tejtatva is Shri Goverdhan to be known as Haridas is also same as Shri Krishna, Vayu tatva is to establish Raslila and Akashtatva is to give the secret meaning of Veds, Sumruthi, Shrimadh Bhagwat Gita and Shri Madh Bhagwatam. He has all the three guan's:-- Saat, Raaj and Tama, i.e.:- Aadibhothik as human being form is Saat * Aadhidevik is Shri Krishna and * Aadiyatimik is Shri Vallabh. * *All the above three Guan are His Swaroops He has graced Vaishnavos by creating various Granths (Books), which give the true picture of Him and Pustimarg.
