Dharma is a duty. We are humans. We live in Society. We are sons and daughters. It is our duty to serve our parents and elders. That is family duty. You may have friends. To help your friends is your duty. That is friendship duty. There are many people, birds and animals living around us. To be helpful to them is our duty. It is human duty. Bharat is our country. To keep our country free, safe and prosperous is our duty. It is called "De-hah-Dharma" or "Rashtra-dharma". We are Citizens, and we act as Citizens, that is called our duty as a citizen. For our own body and life we must strive to maintain good health, study, start earning when we grow up, that is our duty towards ourselves. So, we have so many different duties, which are called dharma. The above mentioned dharmas are related to our body. Our soul has been separated from God. Hence it becomes our duty to seek God and be reunited with him. It is called 'Atma-dharma". It is true Dharma. How did word 'dharma' originate? What does it mean? The word 'dharma' belongs to the Sanskrit language. It is derived from 'duru'. Duru means to bear, to hold, to own. In Sanskrit dharma is elucidated as 'Dharanat dharma'. That which is permanently bearing in one's life is called dharma. Our two main dharmas are Dharma towards mankind and Dharma towards God. To have compassion and to be helpful towards all living beings is our dharma to mankind. To be engaged in the service of God and recitation of God's glory is our dharma towards God. In other languages which are used for 'dharma'? Could you, please elaborate on its meanings ? In English it is 'Religion'. It is derived from the Latin language and its main meaning is 'to join - to unite a separated relationship. 'The atma (soul) has been separated from Parmatma (God) many thousand years ago. That relationship can be reunited by dharma, that is through religion means dharma. In Arabic it is called 'Islam'. Its main meaning is peace That which gives us eternal peace. Only dharma brings peace to man. In Chinese the word is 'Tao". It means the rituals and religious practices in relation to the soul. The rites practiced in order to attain God head-Parmatatma. In Japanese the word is 'Shinto'- which means the Godly path- The path to the eternal. All these words say the same thing. Our main dharma is to attain self-relation to God-head. How many dharmas are there in the world ? There is no determine number. The African tribals and the people of poleregious also have their own dharma. But the main ones are Hindu, Muslim, Christian, Chinese, Tao and Zen of Japanese. In addition to which our country also has Jainism, Buddhism and Sikkhism.

t: If there is only one God, then why are there so many 'dharma to attain Him?
x: There are many roads leading the bazaar, so in the same way there are many 'dharma', which everyone suits an individual, he follows it. There are as many thoughts as there are people and as many thoughts that many dharmas. What is the best dharma? All the roads of the bazaar are good. The one that suit us is the best. The same applies for dharma. All the dharmas are good. No dharma is wrong. The dharma that is convenient for us is the best. What are the main attributes of dharma? Dharma has four main attributes. Sacrifice: To renounce worldly and materialistic attachment. Penance: Self-mortification in order to attain God. Mercy: God exists in every single particle and atom (molecule) in this universe. With that understanding one must have mercy and compassion for all. Never harm anyone. Try and assist others to the best of your ability. Truth: Always speak truth. These are main pillars of all dharma. To imbibe and practise them in life, the paths are different.

Yes, every dharma has sub-religions. We call it 'Sampraday' tradition or custom. Traditional teachings of heirchy of spirtual teachers. What is the name of our religion? It is Sanatan dharma or Ved dharma. It is called sanatan because its tenets are always the same-eternal. Its principal scripture is Ved. So it is called Ved dharma. Our country is Hindustan, So it is known as Hindu dharma. HINDU DHARMA Who established Hindu dharma and when? There is no define set date record, as to its establishment, but it is definitely a very ancient Dharma. In fact to say that, it is the world's oldest religion, would not be wrong. Our ancestors were Aryans and this word in Sanskrit means 'great' since they practiced Santan Dharma. Today we call it hindu dharma. It was not started by anyone, but by God himself, who gave 'Rigved and other Vedas. Which is their main scripture? Hindu dharma has the 'Ved' as its main scripture (religious book). The word Ved is derived from the word 'Vid'. Vid = to know. Ved = knowledge. Which consists the total knowledge of dharma is ved. Ved was not man's work, but they are a creation, manifestaion from God's breath and hence they are considered to be God' words. His words are expressed in this form. It is the world's oldest scripture. However, it was simplified and modified by a great rishi, a saga called Vyasji. Being a wise learned scholar, he categorized it, subjectwise, thus splitting it into 2 section, Uttarkand and Poorvakand. The latter contains information on how to perform yagna to obtain Lord. The former contains, detailed description about God, The Universe, the Soul etc. Since there was a different type of system in ancient times, of no books being written, the guru disciple tradition was one, where the guru spoke, and the disciple heard it and memorized it. But it was not easy to remember the entire recitation. To facilitate this situation, Ved Vyasji made four parts of the Ved. They are Rigved Yajurva Ved Sam Ved Atharva Ved The Sam Ved contains the mantras, which are chanted during Yagnas, while the Atharva Ved contains mantras pertaining to health problems.

It is believed that the Upnishads are also God's creation. They contain the Philosophy of God, Universe, moksha. The word Upnishad, literally means to be able to be close to God or to stay near the Guru, because by studying, you understand God better. Although, in somepeople's opinion, there are nearly 100 upnishads, there are in actuality, approximately 20 main ones. These are the Ishavaasya Upnishad, Ken Upnishad, Chhandogya Upnishad, Mandukya Upnishad, Kath Upnishad etc. Which is the other main religious texts of Hindu Dharma? Ved Vyasji had composed the Brahma Sootra. It is called Vedant. The many Acharyas of hindu dharma have written commentaries on this work, to make it easier to understand. These include the work of Shri Shankaracharyaa, Shri Ramanujacharya, Shri Madhavacharya, Shri Nimbarkacharya and Shri Vallabhacharya. Apart from these which are the other well known scriptures of Hindu Dharma? The Holy Geeta and Bhagvat are the other well known texts. The Geeta is a part of the epic Mahabharat, which Ved Vyasji had written. It is about Shri Krishna's message, a lesson to arjun, on the eve when Kauravas and Pandavas were poised for battle. That is the religious song 'geeta'. Of Vyasji 's 18 Puranas, the main is Bhagvat mahapuran. You must have also heard about 'Ramayan'. It was written by sage Valmiki. What does puran mean? Puran means ancient history. The puranas contain all of the Demigods and their devotees. The main puranas are the Bhagavat, Brahma Puran, Agni Puran, Vayu Puran etc. What is significant about the Hindu Dharma in comparison to other religions? Hindu dharma has its origin in God, not anyone else. The other religions have all been started by great men. Hindu dharma is the world's oldest religions. Its scriptures have not been written by a human being but created by God, in comparison to which, the other religious texts of various religions have been written by their Gurus or priest. Every Hindu is freeto worship God or any Demigod or Demigoddess, according to his faith. In the Hindu dharma, the God and his worship are viewed by the people from different prespectivess, yet there is no clash. Each one is entitled to his own views and faith, while respecting another's. Hindu dharma has many sects. There is no rigidity. Hindu dharma is open to anyone and hence can be practiced by anyone. There is liberty, to do so. BHATKITMARGA(Path of devotion).

t: How many margs (paths) are there in Hindu dharma to Godhead?
x: Mainly three paths are there : Gnan (knowledge), Karma (Rituals) marg means to find out that is missing. Bhakti (devotion) marg To make our intellect pious and by that pious intellect to know our soul and God in gnan marg. It is very difficult. It needs much penance, meditation and yoga. Yagna offering. Vratas, Recitation and Pooja (worship) are rituals. They are also not so easy. To love God heartly, to please him by loving is Bhakti (Devotion). It is very easy and natural. Is Bhakti Marg one or many? Bhakti is 84 types, not one; but mainly two types. Maryada, Pushti. A person offers his Bhakti, to the demigod or demi Goddess as prescripture is Maryada Bhakti. A person offers his selfless divine love to Lord Krishna by doing his Seva, is Pushti Bhakti. Are there sects in Bhakti Marg? Yes, there are main six sects. They all are called Vaishnav Sampraday. Shree Vaishnav Sampraday of Shri Ramamunjacharya. Veer Vaishnav Sampraday of Shri Mashavacharya. Nimbarka Sampraday of Shri Nimbarkacharya. Pushti Sampraday of Shri Vallabacharaya. Goudiya Sampraday of Shri Krishna Chaitanya. Swaminarayan Sampraday of Shri Sahajanand Swami. Over and above these six, Ramanandi Sampraday worships Shri Ram. Other sects worship Shiv, Ganpati, Demi Goddess, Surya etc. They are Shaiv Sampraday, Ganpatya Sampraday, and Shakta Sampraday. PUSHTI SAMPRADAY. (sect) My mother says that our dharma is Hindu, but our sect (sampraday) is Pushti sect. Since you have already explained 'dharma' and Hindu Dharma, please elaborate on 'Sampraday'. What does it mean? 'Sampraday' is a Sanskrit word. It literary means, that which is given well and properly. When God (Bhagvan) comes himself in the form of a great soul on Earth, and he as Bhagvan gives a special Mantra for us, that is called 'Sampraday'. God appeared in the form of Shri Mahaprabhuji, 519 years ago. Then on Shravan sud Ekadashi (agiyarash), God appeared before Shri Mahaprabhuji. It was mid night. He gave Shri Mahaprabhuji the 'Brahma Sambandh' mantra. The Pushti Sampraday has started since then. What does the word 'Pushti' mean? In the Sanskrit language, the words 'pshan, 'pushti' are derivatives from 'push' dhat. The body is maintained by an in take of nourishing food. A person with a strong healthy body is said to be 'pusht'. This can be explained further. When we are small, we are completely taken care of by our mothers. We are quite helpless in managing matters like healthy diet, etc. But Mother loves us, so she takes special tender loving care. This support and help which is provided without any asking is called 'krupa', mercy or compassion. Now this same word 'krupa', in Sanskrit has many meanings. It can mean grace, nourishment, support. This is exactly why our path is know as the Pushti sampraday, because God himself graces us, supports us just the way a child stumbles while learning to walk and his parents help him to stand up and walk; we are unable to do anything to attain God, but God being merciful, bestows his grace on us. He takes care of everything and us and he comes to us. Pushtimarg means the path of grace or support. The path on which, God comes to us, looking for us and bestows His mercy, is called Pushtimarg of Pushti Sampraday.

t: Is it true that in the Pushtimarg, God does every thing? We do not have to do an
x: Is it true that in the Pushtimarg, God does every thing? We do not have to do anything? My mother tells me that I must do seva everyday, do 'jup and path', i.e. recite the verses everyday. It is true. God is the one who controls and does everything. Everything happens only according to the will of God. This is like your mother dear, who cooks in the house, feeds you by putting morsel after morsel in your mouth to nourish you. All of you have to do is chew and swallow, because you don't have pushed it down the gullet - right? You do this because you enjoy it and so does mother . This is exactly what God does to us. He makes us do Seva, Jup, recite the prayers. We derive a certain kind of fulfillment when we do all this. It also makes God very happy. Remember we do not do any of this. It is by God's grace, only, that it is all possible. That is why our sampraday is called Pushtimarg - 'Krupamarg" or the path of grace. What are the main aspects of Pushtimarg? Shri Mahaprabhuji has established Pushtimarg. He is the form of Gods mouth is not different from the body, Shri Mahaprabhuji is not separate from God, neither is He small or less strong. He is God incarnate. A Pushtimargiya Vaishnav must wear a tulsi kanthi around his neck. The Vaishnav men must wear a red tilak on their foreheads. The Vaishnav women must put a red bindi on their foreheads. While doing seva, the men must wear dhoti - bandi (vest) and the women and unmarried girls must wear a sari. You must be intiated with the ashtakshar mantra. If you wish to do Seva, you must also take Brahmasambandh mantra. Lord Krishna is Shri Nathji. we must only worship Him. We must only think of Him and sing His glory. We must not worship any other diety or Goddess. Also, you must take, only Shri Thakorji's prasad. You cannot take any other God or Goddess's prasad. You must do Shri Thakorji's Seva only in your house. You are not to ever, ask God for anything. You must not pray to God for something. Instead, sing the glories of the lord and pray frequently. Make it a habit to do Shri Thakorji's Seva every day. Also do the ashtakasar jup, and all of Yamunaji's verses glorifying her. You must greet everyone with 'Jai Shri Krishna' with love.

Pappa - Mummy say that we are 'Vaishanav'. What is the meaning of 'Vaishnav'? The natives of Bharat are called Bharatiya. Bharatiya is derived from the word 'Bharat'. Similarly from Vishnu comes 'Vaishnav'. The word Vishnu has two meanings. 1. Name of Lord Vishnu 2. Name of demi God Vishnu. The word Vishnu is made from a combination of two words Vish + Anu. Vish=to stay. Anu=the smallest particle. The one who in every minute particle in the world. So the first meaning of Vishnu is God. The one who is a devotee of God is called Vaishnav. One who believes that God exists in every molecule, in the entire universe, is a Vaishnav, Anymate and inanymate, God exists and pervades in all. Having understood that, one who maintains compassion, mercy and love for all, assists others with affection, is a Vaishnav. One who is benevolent but not proud about it, is a Vaishnav. One who does not cause misery and suffering to others, is a Vaishnav. There is another meaning of word Vaishnav. God resides in the entire Universe. God has created the whole universe. God is real. The world that he has created is also real. This creation belongs to God. Hence, we also belong to God. He is our Father. We are his children. A son's duty is to serve his father. Similarly our duty is to serve to God. One who understands this duty and serves God, is a Vaishnav. Shri Krishna is God. Shriji Bava is God. Are Shri Krishna and Shriji Bhavaji one or different? In the pictures they appear different. Why? Shri Krishna and Shriji Bava are one and the same. Shri Krishna who played in Gokul appeared about five hundred years ago form the Govardhan mountain so we call him Shri Govardhan Nathji, we call him Shriji Bava with love. In Vraj language 'Bava' does not mean sadhu. Bava means father or elder. It is true that Shri Krishna and Shriji Bava appear to be different in pictures and paintings. The reason for this is that if you wear a pant-shirt or a dhoti-kafni you are also going to look different in your pictures. The same also applies to Shri Krishna and Shriji Bava. Why should we wear a tulsimala? When you play a cricket match why do you wear a white dress? When you go to school, why do you wear a uniform? The main reason is because that is the rule. The same rule is for Vaishnavas that they must wear a tulsimala. From your uniform people recognize which school you go to. Similarly, a Vaishnav is recognized by his tulsimala. You are proud of your school, when you wear your uniform, you decide mentally that I will not commit any such offence which will tarnish my school's and my reputation. Hence by wearing a tulsimala, we mentally prepare ourselves that I am a Vaishnav. I am doing God's seva as His devotee. I must not indulge in any bad act. I must live like a Vaishnav. Tulsi is God's devotee. She stays in the lotus feet of God in the manner in which Laxmiji and Gangaji are permanently in the service of the lotus feet of God. That is why they are pure and divine. Just by holding tulsi in our hands and on our chest we are inspired with feelings of worship and reverence. Tulsi contains many medicinal qualities. Just by touching it to the body, its medicinal quality has an effect. Shri Mahaprabhuji has given the tulsimala. We are devotees and followers of Shri Mahaprabhuji. That is why it is absolutely necessary to wear it without hesitation and shame. In order to preserve this tulsimala and the tilak on the forehead, Shri Gokulnathji opposed Mogul Emperor Jehangir four hundred years ago. He faced persecution and went on with tulsimala and tilak. It is very important to remember this and put on tulsimala and tilak.

Good thoughts are born less on our intellect and evil thoughts many, so our intellect is like a poisonous Kaliynag. Only Lord Krishna could suppress Kaliya and drove out from the river Yamuna. In the same way only he can control our intellect by putting his lotus like foot on our forehead. Then our intellect will have good and divine thoughts. So Vaishnavs put on Tilak of God's foot shape on their forehead. We should not be ashamed of putting it. Why should we take Charanamrit? Charanamrit consists of sand of Vraj. The bath water of Shri Nathji is added to that sand. The sand of Vraj is divine. The bathwater is also divine. By taking Charanamrit our body, mind and soul become pure and pious. We are eligible for seva. There is soul in every being. When the soul leaves the body, the being dies. What is 'jeev' - soul? How was it born? 'Jeev' means animate, consciousness in its real form. Paramatma decided years ago, to create this universe for his happiness and sport. At that time Paramatma was alone. You need a partner to play with. You also need a playground. So Paramatma, for his own sport created the world (universe) as a playground from Himself. As his playmates, He created innumerable 'jeevs' - being for Himself. So 'jeev' is the smallest form of creation of Paramatma. How was a 'jeev' created from Paramatma? Just the way sparks fly out from a fire, similarly numerous beings spring forth from Paramatma. 'Sat', 'Chit', 'Anand' are the three divine elements in Paramatma, which is why He is called 'Sachidanad'. All the essential elements in the universe, have originated from Paramatma's 'Sat' element. 'Jeev' is a creation of Paramatma's 'Sat' and 'Chit' elements. 'Jeev' is a creation of the combination of 'sat' and 'chit' elements. In the inanimate creation there is no trace of Paramatma's 'anand' element, where as the same 'anand' element is hidden in animate being. But Paramatma manifests his 'anand'.

t: How many types of 'Jeev' (beings, creations) are exist ?
x: According to science there are five types. Those born from sweat or water are subtle being -'Jeev'. Those born from 'Inda' (eggs) are the insects and animal kingdom, and man in the human kingdom. Thus, the origin of beings, have been categorized scientifically. In the Gitaji, Lord Krishna has explained systematically, the essential nature of each one of these being, especially those born in the human kingdom. They can be dichotomized as 'daivi' (pious, blessed souls) and 'asuri' (demonic) 'jeev'. Who can be termed as 'daivi jeev'? 'Daivi' is a derivative from the word 'dev', which in turn is derived from 'divya'. One who has intrinsic values of a 'dev' (demi-God) i.e. divine qualities is called 'daivi jeev'. Such beings are devoted to God and have faith in Him. They have qualities like empathy, gratefulness, and magnanimity, penance, love and affection, forgiveness, peace, non-violence and other such positive qualities. They practise religion specifically to attain God. Shri Mahaprabhuji has further divided 'daivi jeevs' into two types, 'Maryada' and 'Pushti', God has stated various paths in the Vedas and other scriptures, to attain Him. The 'daivi jeev' who follows the paths expounded in these 'shastras' of his own will, is called 'Maryada Jeev'. Such a person lives according to the tenets in the 'Shastras'. There are so many people whom God blesses, himself. Regardless of that person's foibles God the eternal source of mercy, enlightens Him. Such blessed and graced by God Himself are known as 'Pushti Jeev'. Pushti means 'Krupa' or grace. What is the nature of 'asuri' or demonic beings? The people in this world, who are busy enjoying sensual and materialistic pleasure of life, who are possessed with anger, avarice, attachment, violence, inhumanity, deceit and other such amoral traits are 'asuri'. Even though they are sometimes indulging in religious practices, they do it with a selfish motive, without really believing in God. Fifty five percent of the people in the world belong to this type. What type can we Vaishnav be categorized as? Vaishnav are 'Pushti Jeev', because God has created them for the sole purpose of His Seva, so that they must do seva, Shri Mahaprabhuji was sent by God to earth, and was made to give us the Brahmasambandh for doing seva. If Vaishnavs are 'Pushti jeev' then why are so many Vaishnavs in the world, so immersed in enjoying the material world? Why don't they do seva? When a basketful of mangoes contains one rotten mango, the other good mangoes also become rotten. Similarly, we are surrounded by 'asuri jeevs'. We are entrapped in their wrong association. As a consequence we start imitating their false lifestyles and habits. If a good boy from a good family gets involved in a bad company, he becomes a 'gunda' (antisocial element). He forgets his own value-based upbringing. This is exactly what has happened to us. So even though we are Vaishnav pushti jeevs, we are trapped within the confines of the material pleasures. We are unable to engage ourselves in doing seva correctly.

The shashtras have described the size and shape of the 'jeev'. If you take a strand of hair and split into 10,000 fragments, that is the size of a jeev, the smallest subtle fragment. When we die, where does our soul go? It is our body that dies. The soul 'jeev' never dies. Depending on our good and bad karma, we are destined for re-birth. Evil deeds send one to the pittires of hell. But a Vaishnav, who with a love-filled heart, does Shri thakorji's Seva his whole life does not have a rebirth. That soul goes to God's abode, Golok, where there is bliss in the form of Shri Thakorji's seva his whole life does not have a rebirth. Where there is bliss in the form of Shri Thakorji's seva-darshan; the soul attains that 'anand'. This is exactly why we as Vaishnav must do 'Seva' and 'Samaran' (constantly) remembering God. BRAMASAMBANDH What does 'Brahmasambandh' mean? Brahma=Oaramatma. We are embodies souls. Bhagwan Shri Krishna is Paramatma. Many sparks of fire fly out from a fireplace. They are known as a minute particle of the fire. Similarly every jeevatma - embodied soul is - known as a minute particle of Paramatma. A spark of fire away after leaving the fireplace turns to small fragments of coal. If we use it as fuel in the fireplace, it turns into fire. On being separated from its origined or reunited with Paramatma it becomes Paramatma. This reunion of the jeevatma and Paramatma is called Brahmasambandh. Who is the first exponent of this Brahma-sambandh? When was it declared? Lord Krishna himself appeared at midnight on Shravan sud ekadashi, in Gokul. He explained this concept of Brahma - sambandh to Shri Mahaprabhuji and passed on a mantra to achieve this aim. This 5th centenary of the boon of Brahmasambandh. How many letters are contained in Brahma-sambandh Mantra? In which language is it read and given? It has 84 letters. It is in Sanskrit. It's last five letters are known as panchakshar mantra.

t: Will you tell us the meaning of this mantra?
x: Sure. In this mantra the 'jeevatma' introduces itself. It says - I am a part (ansha) of Bhagwan Krishna. I have been separated from him for innumerable years (thousand of years). Hence I have forgotten Bhagwan Krishna completely. I have not felt the need or the thirst to seek Him and reunite with Him. Now I have come to realize that folly, I am such an embodied soul. Then Bhagwan gives his introduction in order to acknowledge and accept the prepared 'jeevatma'. He only uses two words for himself. I am Bhagwan. I act according to my will. One who has a bond of love with me, I protect. I go and meet that devotee. I am Krishna. Krishna means one who has maximum strength. One who is the epitome and embodiment of bliss. I annihilate all the sorrows of one who I accept and take into my fold. I give that devotee every happiness. Once the jeevatma learns about Bhagwan, he pledges in front of Him, 'Oh Krishna! My body, its ten sensory organs, this life, my mind, my husband or wife, my children, my family, my house, all my wealth, all my deeds in this life and in the lives hereafter, along with my 'atma' (soul), I surrender to you. You are a their Master. From today nothing is mine, everything is yours. I will use it in your seva for your happiness. I am your servant. Oh Krishna! I am yours. Who can be initiated with this mantra? Who can give this mantra? In this mantra, the 'jeevatma' pledges in front of Paramatma. One who is willing to fulfill that pledge should be initiated. In other words, after having taken the Brahma-Sambandh pledge, in order to fulfill it, it is necessary that one must do Shri Thakorji's seva. The food (samagri) that one offers Shri Thakorji in seva is the only Prasad that one will eat, is a part of the pledge. Also one should only use what can be offered to Shri Thakorji in seva, as 'prasad'. One Mahaprabhuji's descendant revered Goswami balak are entitled to give this 'diksha'- initiation. How is religious initiation given? Whosoever desires to take this 'diksha' should first be well-informed about the pre and post conditions of taking Brahmasambandh. Then one can go to any revered Goswami 'Balak'. According to their instruction one will have to keep a fast the day previous day. The following day, the person has to go to that particular Goswai balak's house, bathe according to His instructions. Then the person is made to sit in front of Shri Thakorji and a tulsi leaf couplet is given in the one's hand. Then one has to repeat the brahmasambandh mantra. After this Maharajshri will place the tulsi leaf at the lotus feet of Shri Thakorji and Gurudev, and then as per instruction from Gurudev Shri Thakorji's seva must be done. To whom did Shri Mahaprabhuji give the first Brahamsambandh? When was it given? Shri Thakorji ordained Shri Mahaprabhuji to give the Brahamsambandh mantra. The first person was a devotee called Damodardas Harsani. Shri Mahaprabhuji initiated him on shravan sud baras. Hence Shravan sud baras is known as 'Pavitra baras'. In our Pushtimarg, that day is important to us as Guru Purnima. On that day, Vaishnavs offer pavitru and misri to their own Guru, Shri Vallabhkul, at Shri Mahaprabhuji Baithak, and to one's own Shri Thakorji at home. They express their devotion to their Guru. SWAROOP PARICHAY Why do we call Shri Vallabhacharyaji, 'Shri Mahaprabhuji'? 'Prabhu' has two meanings 'Swami' (master) and God. 'Maha' means great. We are God's devotees. A devotee is a subservient devotee of God. God is a devotee's master. Hence, God is our master - 'Prabhu'. Such a lord is subordinate to Shri Vallabhacharyaji. When Shri Vallabhacharyaji accepts a devotee within his fold, He also hands him over to the lord that devotee's hand. Thus, God is attained by Guru Shri Vallabhacharyaji's grace. Therefore, Shri Vallabhacharyaji is the Lord's master. That is why we call him Mahaprabhuji. We are Shri Vallabacharyaji's devotees - sevaks. So he is our Lord and Master. In this world, some are called swami- God (master- H

t: Why is Shri Mahaprabhuji's son Shri Vitthalanathji called Shri Gusaiji?
x: Shri Vitthalnathji had looked after cows a great deal. So the Mughal Emperor Akbar named him 'Goswami' - Lord of the cows. By conferring this title on him, Akbar had honoured Him. So everyone called Him Shri Goswamiji. Words of a language change with time i.e. 'Chandra' become 'Chando'. So Goswami changed to Gusain. All the Vaishnav call him Shri Gusaiji. Goswami become their lineage's new surname. Till Shri Mahaprabhuji's father Shri Laxman Bhattji's time, their surname was 'Bhatt'. Why is Shri Goverdhan- nathji called Shrijibava? Shrijibava is an affectionate name of Shri Goverdhannathji. Just way, your name is Taral, but at home they call you 'Taru'. Where is love, the name is shortened. Shri Govardhannathji was shortened to Shri Nathji. Shri Nathji became Shriji. In Vraj language, 'bava' implies respect. In Gujarati it means a sage, but in Vraj language, an elder is called 'bava'. So we call Shri Goverdhannathji, Shriji - bava. Why is Shri Yamunaji called Shri Maharani? There are many gopies in Vraj. They all love Shri Krishna. We all know that friendship is built with like-minded people. They form a group. Similarly there are four main groups of Gopies in Vraj. Every group has a leader. So each of these four groups has a main Gopi. She is very dear to Lord Krishna. That is why she is called Shri Swaminiji. Shri Radhikaji, Shri Chandravaliji , Shri Radha-Sahehariji and Shri Yamunaji are the four main Gopies - Swaminiji. As much as Shri Yamunaji loves Shri Krishana, She love the Gopies and all devotee as much. She does not have any trace of selfishness in her. Others happiness make her happy. That is why she is called 'Maharani'. What does the word 'Vraj' mean? In Sanskrit language 'Vraj' has many meanings & e.g. Motion, entry, A small village, A forest, abode of shepherd's huts. The villages Vraj and Nandraiji has to keep moving from place to place, to seek fresh pastures for their cows. Therefore they had no permanent home. So they called this place Vraj. These Vrajvasis (natives of Vraj) lived in straw and mud huts. They called it Vrajbhoomi (land). These small husts formed into villages and they called it Vraj. Shri Krishna used to roam all over this land, with his friends and cows, because of their movements, it was called 'Vraj'.

t: Is there one or are there many Vrindavans in Vraj?
x: There are 4 spots known as Vrindavan in Vraj Chandra Sarovar, Which is known as Adi Vrindavan. It is at the base of Shri Giriraj. Kamvan is also known as Bag Vrindavan. The present Vrindavan is known as Vasant Vrindavan. The surrounding area of Nandgaun is known as Central Vrindavan. In all these 4 places Shri Krishna has done [gaucharan and played Ras) . What is Shrinathji's Charachowki? From Vraj, Shrinathji went to Mewar (Nathdwara). On the way there he halted at several places. All these places, starting from Shri Giriraj to Shri Nathdwara, are called his 'Charanchowki'. With the 'bhav' that Shriji still dwells in these places, his seva is done in each and every place. BAITHAKJI What is the meaning of the word ' baithak'? In ordinary colloquial parlance, the word 'baithak', means a place to sit. When there is a music programme, it is called 'sangeet (music) baithak'. When kings used to meet with their ministers and noblemen to discuss important matters, that was also called a 'baithak'. In our 'Pushtimarg' the word 'baithak' is not used in this context. Then what does it mean? You all know that Shri Mahaprabhuji is the founder of our 'Pushtimarg'. You also know that He started His pilgrimage (yatra) of Bharat, at the age of 11 years. As you are aware that he always walked barefoot. He walked extensively from Badrinath to Himalayas, Rameshwar in the South, Jagannath Puri in the East and Dwarka in the West. This, he accomplished thrice in his life time, on barefoot with certain vows. During the time between these yatras, He usually preferred to camp out in the open. He used to choose a place on the outskirts of a village or town. A place which was close to a river or lake, and he would rest under a tree, so, as you can see, he loved Nature and a peaceful environment. Now, in many of these place, He used to read the Bhagvat, as a 'Parayan'. This would take at least 3 to 7 days. In many places He had also read Valmiki's Ramayan, and the holy Geeta. This reading of religious books before an audience or alone within a limited period is called 'parayan'. Shri Mahaprabhuji stayed for longer periods at most of these places and did 'parayan'. It is the place, the particular spot, where he did 'parayan', is called 'baithak'. What is the total number of Shri Maha-Prabhuji's 'baithaks'? Totally there are 84 well known baithaks of Shri Mahaprabhuji. But after reading his biography, we understand that there are more than 84 baithaks.

t: Who made these 'baithaks' of Shri Mahaprabhuji open to public?
x: Shri Gokulnathji was Shri Mahaprabhuji's grandson. It is his credit, that we have so much information about the baithaks. He had written a book in Vraj language. It is called 'Baithak Charitra'. This book contains interesting stories of baithaks. A noteworthy incident has taken place at each one of these 'baithaks'. The book is a compilation of all these stories. It is the oldest known recorded history about detailed literature on the 84 'baithaks'. It dates back to 400 years. Are these 'baithaks' still evident today? No. Most of these 'baithaks are open today. The rest are not visible and these are mainly in South India. What does a 'baithak' consist of? Firstly, the spot where Shri Mahaprabhuji had sat, is marked by a mud square. Today in some of these spots, a marble slab has been placed. These spots are worshipped with the image of Shri Mahaprabhuji in mind-as He still sits there. In many places, they apply tilak, offer tulsi kanthi and dhoti - uperna. In some baithak's a 'gadi' (small mattress) and takiya(pillow) are placed. A tilak is made on the pillow-'takiya', and 'Shringar' are also offered. Dhoti and uperna are also a part of the offering. In some 'baithaks' Shri Mahaprabhuji's picture is also placed on the 'gaditakiya'. Who can do seva in the 'baithak'? Only those vaishnavs, who have been initiated with the Brahmasambandh mantra, can do seva in the 'baithak'. They have to bathe and remain in 'app-ras' (without touching anything impure) if they want to do seva. What is the significance of and why is it important to fill 'jhari ji' in the 'baithak'? It is important to remember that Pushtimarg is not only for the rich. The poorest of the poor can become a vaishanav. Shri Mahaprabhuji does not discriminate between vaishnavs. The seva of 'jhari' not entail any expense whatsoever. It is possible, even for the most poor vaishnav. When you spend more money, you become arrogant. So, since there is no expense involved in filiing the jhari one does not become proud. There is no place for false pride in Pushtimarg. Rather, its primary requirements are mercy and kindness. Thus, when vaishnav go to the baithak to fill 'jhari', they experience compassion and mercy, not pride. How do we fill the jhari in the 'baithak'? The way in which the 'mukhiyaji' instructs you. In case there are too many vaishnavs, to fill jhari, they should put their right hand on the vaishnav's right shoulder (i.e. the vaishnav standing exactly in front of them). Then with eyes shut, and reciting the Yamunashtak mentally or orally, each vaishnav must fulfil his desire to fill jhari. Are there any other baithaks besides Shri Mahaprahbuji's? Yes, the other baithaks are of Shri Gusainji, his seven sons, Shri Hariraiji, Shri Nathji and Shri Damodardas Harsaniji. Their total number is 58. so 84 + 58 = 142 baithaks.

We go to haveli for darshan. But when we do not get darshan, what do we do? First let us understand, whose darshan are we going for? Thakorji is in the haveli and in our homes. Thakorji is the Supreme Reality, not some ordinary swaroop. Haveli is 'Nandalay' (Nandbava's house). Shri Kanhaiyalal as child Krishna, and dearest to Shri Nandbava and Shri Yashodama stays there. We go for that divine and unearthly swarup's darshan. The gopis used to go every morning to Nandbava's house for Balkrishna's darshan. They could not bear to stay away from his darshan. We must all keep the same bhavna when we go for darshan. Secondly, the Haveli is Shri Nandraiji's house. He is the king of Vraj, and for a very big man. If we go his house, we must behave in a certain manner. If it is not time for darshan, then we have to sit cross legged and wait in the country yard. Thirdly, we must not indulge in idle gossip, while waiting. Remember, not to shout or make a loud noise. Instead, mentally you must recite the Ashtakshar Mantra. Shri Yamunashtak also be recited. In a soft tone you can sing 'dholpad.' What are the other restrictions, while we are in the Haveli? You cannot put your fingers in your mouth. No spitting. You cannot sit anywhere and eat and drink. After having eaten or drunk water wash hands immediately. Do not touch your hands everywhere. Do not fight with anyone. You cannot greet another Vaishnav by saying 'Jai Shri Krishna' in front of Shri Thakorji. Now without having asked, remember this is of utmotst importance. By doing darshan we get happiness. But if we do Shri Thakorji's seva in our house, then there is double happiness. You are also happy and Shri Thakorji is also happy. That happiness is a great deal more than that of the Haveli. So be sure to keep Shri Thakorji in your house and do seva. > ASHTAKSHARMANTRA What is the meaning of 'Shri Krishna Sharnam Mama'? 'Shri Krishna Sharnam Mama' means Shri Krishna is my refuge, shelter. In Sanskrit, one of the meanings of 'sharan' is protector. One who protects us, is the protector. Shri Krishna is my protector means Shri Krishna is the one who protects me. Only the one who is himself powerful can protect other. Shri Krishna is God, that is why, he is the most powerful in the world. There is none who can compare or compete with him. So if Lord Krishna becomes our protector then we need fear no-one. We become fearless. For this reason, Shri Maha-prabhuji has given us the 'Shri Krishna Sharnam Mama' mantra. What does mantra mean? Mantra means that which can be whispered in the ear, a secret. Sages (rishi-munis), saints, religious heads were all told God's own secret by God Himself. That is called a mantra. The mantra contains God's own spiritual name. It is very pure. Who we make our guru tells us the gurumantra in our ear. Shri Mahaprabhuji has given us an Ashtakshar-mantra which is 'Shri Krishna Sharnam Mama'. Back to Ashtakshar Maha Mantra Page

There are eight words contained in it, that is why it is called 'Ashtakshar mantra'. In our Pushti-Marg it is also called 'nam-mantra', because it embodies God's name. How is this mantra supposed to be spoken? There are three ways of reciting this mantra. Loudly, so that others can hear. With just lip movement, so that it is not audible to other, Mentally without any lip movement. The third one is the best one. The mantra should be mused mentally. Where can one recite this mantra? Others mantras are chanted after a bath, and after wearing clean clothes by sitting on an asan. The Ashtakshar mantra can be chanted similarly. There is no rigid ritual to recite it. You can muse it while undertaking any of these activities, walking, strolling, eating-drinking, playing, sleeping, waking. You can recite it constantly. Is there any other mantra, besides this one, which can be recited? If our gurus gives us a mantra, that can be recited. There are many mantras. But you cannot recite them all. Pushtimarg has advocated Ashtakshar Brahmasambandh mantra. These two mantras have been given to us by our Gurudev, so we must recite them. Every morning, after by bath, you must (recite) do one jap mala, at least once of this mantra. How many times would be doing this mantra if we complete one round? There are 108 beads in one mala (rosary; not necklace). Hence if you complete one round of the mala you will have done the jap of the mantra 108 times. In case you do not have access to a japmala, you can count on your fingers and complete one round. Is there any specific method of using this jupmala? Yes. The knot in the mala is called 'meru'. The jup starts with bead after that meru. The bead is to be held between the thumb and the middle finger. The forefinger (the one between the thumb and middle finger) should not touch the bead. The bead should be facing your chest. When one round is complete, the meru should not be crossed over. Turn the mala around, and restart the next round. Back to Ashtakshar Maha Mantra Page

The coverage of Shri Pushti Sampradhay in this website is purely extract from ||Achariya-charan Shri Madh Vallabh’s|| Pusti Marg and its principles are doctrined by Shri Vallabh's Grace and Shri Thakurji's Free will. ||Shri Vallabh's|| various granths (books) are base of it, ||Shri Vithalnathji|| added more depth to it through his granths (books). The Varta Sahitiyah {actual happening's written as stories for the knowledge and remembrance of future generations} these manuscript's, though rare speak antiquity, factual happening's in an structured traditional manner. Other works by Shri Gokulnathji and his granths too have been taken. Shri Hariraiji Mahaprabhuji’s granths have also graced us with the information. We all pusti jives [Vaishnavs] are indebt to their blessing and Grace and must always remain obliged. Hence our duty is to follow Their path of Pustimarg and its principles. All the works of Pushti Margh Start and end on one note, "To serve Shri Krishna and Shri Krishna alone, while so doing, be in oneness with him, yet remaining his das (servant). Serving him all day long and still carving for more. Knowing this and being sublime in your thoughts and actions renouncing all desires to be for him". We are grateful to following Vallabh-kul-balaks and anubhavi Vaishnavas to whom we genuflect, whose writing can be read on this site. They are: Goswami Shri Dwarkeshlalji – Kadi, Ahmedabad . Goswami Shri Dwarkeshji – Kandivli,Champaranya, Amreli, Surat, Amedabad. Goswami Shri Prathameshji Maharaj. And many more whose names are not Mentioned here. Viewers and interested readers are requested inform us about any thing, wrongly written or presented understood or otherwise so that we can learn and correct. We shall remain highly obliged. DANDVRAT PRANAM

With love and honour I bow down to the always merciful Feet of my Guru-Dwar, Jagat-Guru Shri-Madh-Vallabh-Acha-riya Pradhan-pithistith, Aacha-riya-vairiya nitya-lila-asth Tilka-yat Shri 108 Shri Govind-lal-ji Mahraj-shri whose Blessing has brought me into this Graceful Sampradaya and whose teachings has enabled me to say few words of glory of Pusti Sampra-daya. I bow down always to my one and only GURUDEV, Shri Jagat-Guru Shri-Madh-Vallabh-Acha-riya-ji, Shri Goverdhan-dharan Shri Thakur-ji Shri Nathji, Shri Param Kripalu Kalindi-ji (the always ready to bless its devotees) Shri Yamuna-ji and solicit their kripa on me and my family .......[navin ramdas]. My Family Background: My Grandfather Shri Tarachandji and his brother Shri Jethanandji were sons of my Great Grandfather Shri Godha-malji, who lived in Thatta- Sind. Shri Tarachandji and his wife Shri Bulabai, were very highy learned Vaishnav, and at the same time humble and down to earth people. I can say them, they were in real sense 'Unch Koti Vaishnav' {Vaishnav of higher dimension} they had 2 sons Shri Keshavdasji and my father Shri Ramdasji. They also had a daughter Shri Tulsabai. Shri Tarachand left this world and went to Shri Krishna's kripaful Abode at a very early age. His sister Shri Tulsabai also became widow at very young age. Both mother Shri Bulabai and daughter Shri Tulsabai renounced everything and went to Shri Nathdwara, Rajasthan, to settle there. Both of them are remembered till date by plenty many Vaishnav's not only in Nathdwara but also by my community people and other vaishnav associated with them either through time or Vaishnavta. Their blessing on me and my family have provided me the platform to bear the fruit of this Pusti Sampra-daya .......[navin ramdas] Objective: Our aim behind constructing this website is praising Bhagwan Shri Krishna whilst so doing we also want to enlighten the hearts of the youth [both young at heart and age] about our Pushti Sampra-daya and to bridge the gap between the 'Knower' and the 'New-comer' and also the 'Inquisitive Learner' about Pushti-Margh.
